judgment.zh_hant: 元亨，利貞。至于八月有凶。
judgment.zh_hans: 元亨，利贞。至于八月有凶。
judgment.en_legge: Lin (indicates that under the conditions supposed in it) there will be great progress and success, while it will be advantageous to be firmly correct. In the eighth month there will be evil.

tuan.zh_hant: 臨，剛浸而長，說而順，剛中而應。大亨以正、天之道也。至于八月有凶、消不久也。
tuan.zh_hans: 临，刚浸而长，说而顺，刚中而应。大亨以正、天之道也。至于八月有凶、消不久也。
tuan.en_legge: In Lin (we see) the strong (lines) gradually increasing and advancing. (The lower trigram is the symbol of) being pleased, and (the upper of) being compliant. The strong (line) is in the central position, and is properly responded to. 'There is great progress and success, along with firm correctness:'—this is the way of Heaven. 'In the eighth month there will be evil:'—(the advancing power) will decay after no long time.

image.zh_hant: 澤上有地，臨。君子以教思无窮，容保民无疆。
image.zh_hans: 泽上有地，临。君子以教思无穷，容保民无疆。
image.en_legge: (The trigram for) the waters of a marsh and that for the earth above it form Lin. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his purposes of instruction that are inexhaustible, and nourishes and supports the people without limit.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject advancing in company (with the subject of the second line). Through his firm correctness there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune through the firm correctness of (the subject of the first line) advancing in company (with the subject of the second)' is due to his will being set on doing what is right.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject advancing in company (with the subject of the first line). There will be good fortune; (advancing) will be in every way advantageous.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 咸臨吉无不利、未順命也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 咸临吉无不利、未顺命也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune and every possible advantage attending the advance (of the subject of the second line), in company (with the subject of the first),' arises from the fact that those (to whom the advance is made) are not yet obedient to the ordinances (of Heaven).

text.zh_hant: 甘臨，无攸利；既憂之，无咎。
text.zh_hans: 甘临，无攸利；既忧之，无咎。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows one well pleased (indeed) to advance, (but whose action) will be in no way advantageous. If he become anxious about it (however), there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 甘臨、位不當也，既憂之、咎不長也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 甘临、位不当也，既忧之、咎不长也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He (shows himself) well pleased to advance:'—his position is not that appropriate to him. 'If he become anxious, however, about his action,' his error will not be continued.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows one advancing in the highest mode. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The freedom from error consequent on the advance in the highest mode' is due to the (various) appropriateness of the position.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows the advance of wisdom, such as befits the great ruler. There will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'What befits the great ruler' means the pursuing the course of the due mean.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows the advance of honesty and generosity. There will be good fortune, and no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune consequent on the advance of honesty and generosity' is due to the will (of the subject of the line) being set on the subjects of (the first two lines of) the inner (trigram).

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Kwan shows (how he whom it represents should be like) the worshipper who has washed his hands, but not (yet) presented his offerings;—with sincerity and an appearance of dignity (commanding reverent regard).

tuan.zh_hant: 大觀在上，順而巽，中正以觀天下，觀。盥而不薦、有孚顒若、下觀而化也，觀天之神道而四時不忒。聖人以神道設教而天下服矣。
tuan.zh_hans: 大观在上，顺而巽，中正以观天下，观。盥而不荐、有孚颙若、下观而化也，观天之神道而四时不忒。圣人以神道设教而天下服矣。
tuan.en_legge: The great Manifester occupies an upper place (in the figure), which consists of (the trigrams whose attributes are) docility and flexibility. He is in the central position and his correct place, and thus exhibits (his lessons) to all under heaven. 'Kwan shows its subject like a worshipper who has washed his hands, but not (yet) presented his offerings;—with sincerity and an appearance of dignity (commanding reverent regard):'—(all) beneath look to him and are transformed. When we contemplate the spirit-like way of Heaven, we see how the four seasons proceed without error. The sages, in accordance with (this) spirit-like way, laid down their instructions, and all under heaven yield submission to them.

image.zh_hant: 風行地上，觀。先王以省方觀民設教。
image.zh_hans: 风行地上，观。先王以省方观民设教。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) the earth, and that for wind moving above it, form Kwan. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, examined the (different) regions (of the kingdom), to see the (ways of the) people, and set forth their instructions.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows the looking of a lad;—not blamable in men of inferior rank, but matter for regret in superior men.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The looking of a lad shown by the first line, divided,' indicates the way of the inferior people.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one peeping out from a door. It would be advantageous if it were (merely) the firm correctness of a female.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The firm correctness of a woman, in peeping out from a door 'is also a thing to be ashamed of (in a superior man).

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows one looking at (the course of) his own life, to advance or recede (accordingly).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He looks at (the course of) his own life, to advance or recede (accordingly):'—he will not err in the path (to be pursued).

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows one contemplating the glory of the kingdom. It will be advantageous for him, being such as he is, (to seek) to be a guest of the king.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He contemplates the glory of the kingdom:'—(thence) arises the wish to be a guest (at court).

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his own life(-course). A superior man, he will (thus) fall into no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He contemplates his own life(-course):'—he should (for this purpose) contemplate (the condition of) the people.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows its subject contemplating his character to see if it be indeed that of a superior man. He will not fall into error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He contemplates his own character:'—he cannot even yet let his mind be at rest.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Shih Ho indicates successful progress (in the condition of things which it supposes). It will be advantageous to use legal constraints.

tuan.zh_hant: 頤中有物曰噬嗑。噬嗑而亨，剛柔分，動而明，雷電合而章。柔得中而上行，雖不當位，利用獄也。
tuan.zh_hans: 颐中有物曰噬嗑。噬嗑而亨，刚柔分，动而明，雷电合而章。柔得中而上行，虽不当位，利用狱也。
tuan.en_legge: The existence of something between the jaws gives rise to the name Shih Ho (Union by means of biting through the intervening article). The Union by means of biting through the intervening article indicates 'the successful progress (denoted by the hexagram).' The strong and weak (lines) are equally divided (in the figure). Movement is denoted (by the lower trigram), and bright intelligence (by the upper); thunder and lightning uniting in them, and having brilliant manifestation. The weak (fifth) line is in the centre, and acts in its high position. Although it is not in its proper position, this is advantageous for the use of legal constraints.

image.zh_hant: 雷電噬嗑。先王以明罰勑法。
image.zh_hans: 雷电噬嗑。先王以明罚𠡠法。
image.en_legge: (The trigrams representing) thunder and lightning form Shih Ho. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, framed their penalties with intelligence, and promulgated their laws.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows one with his feet in the stocks and deprived of his toes. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'His feet are in the stocks, and he is deprived of his toes:'—there is no walking (to do evil).

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one biting through the soft flesh, and (going on to) bite off the nose. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He bites through the soft flesh, and (goes on) to bite off the nose:'—(the subject of the line) is mounted on the strong (first line).

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows one gnawing dried flesh, and meeting with what is disagreeable. There will be occasion for some small regret, but no (great) error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He meets with what is disagreeable and hurtful:'—his position is not the proper one for him.

text.zh_hant: 噬乾胏，得金矢。利艱貞、吉。
text.zh_hans: 噬乾胏，得金矢。利艰贞、吉。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows one gnawing the flesh dried on the bone, and getting the pledges of money and arrows. It will be advantageous to him to realise the difficulty of his task and be firm,—in which case there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'It will be advantageous to him to realise the difficulty of his task and be firm, in which case there will be good fortune:'—his light has not yet been sufficiently displayed.

text.zh_hant: 噬乾肉，得黃金。貞厲无咎。
text.zh_hans: 噬乾肉，得黄金。贞厉无咎。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows one gnawing at dried flesh, and finding the yellow gold. Let him be firm and correct, realising the peril (of his position). There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Let him be firm and correct, realising the peril (of his position), and there will be no error:'—he will possess every quality appropriate (to his position and task).

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows one wearing the cangue, and deprived of his ears. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He wears the cangue and is deprived of his ears:'—he hears, but will not understand.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Pi indicates that there should be free course (in what it denotes). There will be little advantage (however) if it be allowed to advance (and take the lead).

tuan.zh_hant: 賁亨，柔來而文剛，故亨。分剛上而文柔，故小利有攸往。剛柔交錯、天文也。文明以止，人文也。觀乎天文以察時變，觀乎人文以化成天下。
tuan.zh_hans: 贲亨，柔来而文刚，故亨。分刚上而文柔，故小利有攸往。刚柔交错、天文也。文明以止，人文也。观乎天文以察时变，观乎人文以化成天下。
tuan.en_legge: (When it is said that) Pi indicates that there should be free course (in what it denotes):—(We see) the weak line coming and ornamenting the strong lines (of the lower trigram), and hence (it is said that ornament) 'should have free course.' On the other hand, the strong line above ornaments the weak ones (of the upper trigram), and hence (it is said) that 'there will be little advantage, if (ornament) be allowed to advance (and take the lead).' (This is illustrated in the) appearances that ornament the sky. Elegance and intelligence (denoted by the lower trigram) regulated by the arrest (denoted by the upper) suggest the observances that adorn human (society). We look at the ornamental figures of the sky, and thereby ascertain the changes of the seasons. We look at the ornamental observances of society, and understand how the processes of transformation are accomplished all under heaven.

image.zh_hant: 山下有火，賁。君子以明庶政，无敢折獄。
image.zh_hans: 山下有火，贲。君子以明庶政，无敢折狱。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a mountain and that for fire under it form Pi. The superior man, in accordance with this, throws a brilliancy around his various processes of government, but does not dare (in a similar way) to decide cases of criminal litigation.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows one adorning (the way of) his feet. He can discard a carriage and walk on foot.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He can discard a carriage and walk on foot:'—righteousness requires that he should not ride.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one adorning his beard.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He adorns his beard:'—he rouses himself to action (only) along with the (subject of the) line above.

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of being adorned and bedewed (with rich favours). But let him ever maintain his firm correctness, and there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune consequent on his ever maintaining firm correctness' is due to this,—that to the end no one will insult him.

text.zh_hant: 賁如皤如，白馬翰如，匪寇，婚媾。
text.zh_hans: 贲如皤如，白马翰如，匪寇，婚媾。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows one looking as if adorned, but only in white. As if (mounted on) a white horse, and furnished with wings, (he seeks union with the subject of the first line), while (the intervening third pursues), not as a robber, but intent on a matrimonial alliance.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 六四、當位疑也，匪寇婚媾、終无尤也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 六四、当位疑也，匪寇婚媾、终无尤也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The place occupied by the fourth line, divided,' affords ground for doubt (as to its subject); but '(as the subject of the third pursues) not as a robber, but as intent on a matrimonial alliance,' he will in the end have no grudge against him.

text.zh_hant: 賁于丘園，束帛戔戔，吝終吉。
text.zh_hans: 贲于丘园，束帛戋戋，吝终吉。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows its subject adorned by (the occupants of) the heights and gardens. He bears his roll of silk, small and slight. He may appear stingy; but there will be good fortune in the end.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune falling to the fifth line, divided,' affords occasion for joy.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows one with white as his (only) ornament. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The freedom from error attached to (the subject of) the topmost line, with no ornament but the (simple white),' shows how he has attained his aim.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Po indicates that (in the state which it symbolises) it will not be advantageous to make a movement in any direction whatever.

tuan.zh_hant: 剝、剝也。柔變剛也。不利有攸往、小人長也。順而止之，觀象也。君子尚消息盈虛，天行也。
tuan.zh_hans: 剥、剥也。柔变刚也。不利有攸往、小人长也。顺而止之，观象也。君子尚消息盈虚，天行也。
tuan.en_legge: Po denotes overthrowing or being overthrown. We see (in the figure) the weak lines (threatening to) change the (last) strong line (into one of themselves), That 'it will not be advantageous to make a movement in any direction whatever' appears from the fact that the small men are (now) growing and increasing. The superior man acts according to (the exigency of the time), and stops all forward movement, looking at the (significance of the) symbolic figures (in the hexagram). He values the processes of decrease and increase, of fulness and decadence, (as seen) in the movements of the heavenly bodies.

image.zh_hant: 山附於地，剝。上以厚下安宅。
image.zh_hans: 山附于地，剥。上以厚下安宅。
image.en_legge: (The trigrams representing) the earth, and (above it) that for a mountain, which adheres to the earth, form Po. Superiors, in accordance with this, seek to strengthen those below them, to secure the peace and stability of their own position.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows one overturning the couch by injuring its legs. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He overthrows the couch by injuring its legs:'—thus (he commences) his work of ruin with what is lowest (in the superior man).

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one overthrowing the couch by injuring its frame. (The injury will go on to) the destruction of (all) firm correctness, and there will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He destroys the couch by injuring its frame:'—(the superior man) has as yet no associates.

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject among the overthrowers; but there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: That 'there will be no error on the part of this one among the overthrowers' arises from the difference between him and the others above and below.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject having overthrown the couch, and (going to injure) the skin (of him who lies on it). There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He has overthrown the couch, and (proceeds to injure) the skin (of him who lies on it):'-—calamity is very near at hand.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows (its subject leading on the others like) a string of fishes, and (obtaining for them) the favour that lights on the inmates of the palace. There will be advantage in every way.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He obtains for them the favour that lights on the inmates of the palace:'—in the end there will be no grudge against him.

text.zh_hant: 碩果不食，君子得輿，小人剝廬。
text.zh_hans: 硕果不食，君子得舆，小人剥庐。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject (as) a great fruit which has not been eaten. The superior man finds (the people again) as a chariot carrying him. The small men (by their course) overthrow their own dwellings.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 君子得輿、民所載也，小人剝廬、終不可用也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 君子得舆、民所载也，小人剥庐、终不可用也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The superior man finds himself in a carriage:'—he is carried along by the people. 'The small men (by their course) overthrow their own dwellings:'—they can never again be of use to them.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 亨。出入无疾。朋來无咎。反復其道，七日來復。利有攸往。
judgment.zh_hans: 亨。出入无疾。朋来无咎。反复其道，七日来复。利有攸往。
judgment.en_legge: Fu indicates that there will be free course and progress (in what it denotes). (The subject of it) finds no one to distress him in his exits and entrances; friends come to him, and no error is committed. He will return and repeat his (proper) course. In seven days comes his return. There will be advantage in whatever direction movement is made.

tuan.zh_hant: 復亨。剛反動而以順行。是以出入无疾、朋來无咎。反復其道、七日來復，天行也。利有攸往、剛長也。復、其見天地之心乎。
tuan.zh_hans: 复亨。刚反动而以顺行。是以出入无疾、朋来无咎。反复其道、七日来复，天行也。利有攸往、刚长也。复、其见天地之心乎。
tuan.en_legge: 'Fu indicates the free course and progress (of what it denotes):'—it is the coming back of what is intended by the undivided line. (Its subject's) actions show movement directed by accordance with natural order. Hence 'he finds no one to distress him in his exits and entrances,' and 'friends come to him, and no error is committed.' 'He will return and repeat his proper course; in seven days comes his return:'—such is the movement of the heavenly (revolution). 'There will be advantage in whatever direction movement is made:'—the strong lines are growing and increasing. Do we not see in Fu the mind of heaven and earth?

image.zh_hant: 雷在地中，復。先王以至日閉關，商旅不行，后不省方。
image.zh_hans: 雷在地中，复。先王以至日闭关，商旅不行，后不省方。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for thunder in the midst of it form Fu. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, on the day of the (winter) solstice, shut the gates of the passes (from one state to another), so that the travelling merchants could not (then) pursue their journeys, nor the princes go on with the inspection of their states.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject returning (from an error) of no great extent, which would not proceed to anything requiring repentance. There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Returning (from an error) of no great extent' is the prelude to the cultivation of the person.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows the admirable return (of its subject), There will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune attendant on the admirable return (of the subject of the second line)' is due to his condescension to the virtuous (subject of the line) below.

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows one who has made repeated returns. The position is perilous, but there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: Notwithstanding 'the perilous position of him who has made many returns,' there will be no error through (his aiming after righteousness).

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject moving right in the centre (among those represented by the other divided lines), and yet returning alone (to his proper path).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He moves right in the centre (among those represented by the other divided lines), and yet returns alone:'—his object is to pursue the (proper) path.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows the noble return of its subject. There will be no ground for repentance.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The noble return, giving no ground for repentance,' is due to (the subject of the line) striving to perfect himself in accordance with his central position.

text.zh_hant: 迷復，凶，有災眚。用行師，終有大敗，以其國君凶，至于十年不克征。
text.zh_hans: 迷复，凶，有灾眚。用行师，终有大败，以其国君凶，至于十年不克征。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject all astray on the subject of returning. There will be evil. There will be calamities and errors. If with his views he put the hosts in motion, the end will be a great defeat, whose issues will extend to the ruler of the state. Even in ten years he will not be able to repair the disaster.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The evil consequent on being all astray on the subject of returning' is because the course pursued is contrary to the proper course for a ruler.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 元亨，利貞。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。
judgment.zh_hans: 元亨，利贞。其匪正有眚，不利有攸往。
judgment.en_legge: Wu Wang indicates great progress and success, while there will be advantage in being firm and correct. If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction.

tuan.zh_hant: 无妄，剛自外來而為主於內，動而健，剛中而應。大亨以正，天之命也。其匪正有眚、不利有攸往，无妄之往何之矣？天命不祐，行矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 无妄，刚自外来而为主于内，动而健，刚中而应。大亨以正，天之命也。其匪正有眚、不利有攸往，无妄之往何之矣？天命不祐，行矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: In Wu Wang we have the strong (first) line come from the outer (trigram), and become in the inner trigram lord (of the whole figure); we have (the attributes of) motive power and strength; we have the strong line (of the fifth place) in the central position, and responded to (by the weak second):—there will be 'great progress proceeding from correctness;' such is the appointment of Heaven. 'If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction:'—whither can he (who thinks he is) free from all insincerity, (and yet is as here described) proceed? Can anything be done (advantageously) by him whom the (will and) appointment of Heaven do not help?

image.zh_hant: 天下雷行，物與无妄。先王以茂對時育萬物。
image.zh_hans: 天下雷行，物与无妄。先王以茂对时育万物。
image.en_legge: The thunder rolls all under the sky, and to (every)thing there is given (its nature), free from all insincerity. The ancient kings, in accordance with this, (made their regulations) in complete accordance with the seasons, thereby nourishing all things.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject free from all insincerity. His advance will be accompanied with good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: When 'he who is free from insincerity makes any movement,' he will get what he desires.

text.zh_hant: 不耕穫；不菑畬；則利有攸往。
text.zh_hans: 不耕获；不菑畬；则利有攸往。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one who reaps without having ploughed (that he might reap), and gathers the produce of his third year's fields without having cultivated them the first year for that end. To such a one there will be advantage in whatever direction he may move.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He reaps without having ploughed:'—(the thought of) riches to be got had not risen (in his mind).

text.zh_hant: 无妄之災，或繫之牛，行人之得，邑人之災。
text.zh_hans: 无妄之灾，或系之牛，行人之得，邑人之灾。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows calamity happening to one who is free from insincerity;—as in the case of an ox that has been tied up. A passer by finds it (and carries it off), while the people in the neighbourhood have the calamity (of being accused and apprehended).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The passer-by gets the ox:'—this proves a calamity to the people of the neighbourhood.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows (a case) in which, if its subject can remain firm and correct, there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'If he can remain firm and correct there will be no error:'—he firmly holds fast (his correctness).

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows one who is free from insincerity, and yet has fallen ill. Let him not use medicine, and he will have occasion for joy (in his recovery).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Medicine in the case of one who is free from insincerity!'—it should not be tried (at all).

text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject free from insincerity, yet sure to fall into error, if he take action. (His action) will not be advantageous in any way.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The action (in this case) of one who is free from insincerity' will occasion the calamity arising from action (when the time for it is) exhausted.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 利貞。不家食吉。利涉大川。
judgment.zh_hans: 利贞。不家食吉。利涉大川。
judgment.en_legge: Under the conditions of Ta Khu it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (If its subject do not seek to) enjoy his revenues in his own family (without taking service at court), there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous for him to cross the great stream.

tuan.zh_hant: 大畜，剛健篤實，煇光日新。其德剛上而尚賢，能止健，大正也，不家食吉、養賢也，利涉大川、應乎天也。
tuan.zh_hans: 大畜，刚健笃实，𪸩光日新。其德刚上而尚贤，能止健，大正也，不家食吉、养贤也，利涉大川、应乎天也。
tuan.en_legge: In (the trigrams composing) Ta Khu we have (the attributes) of the greatest strength and of substantial solidity, which emit a brilliant light; and indicate a daily renewal of his virtue (by the subject of it). The strong line is in the highest place, and suggests the value set on talents and virtue; there iS power (in the upper trigram) to keep the strongest in restraint:—all this shows 'the great correctness' (required in the hexagram). 'The good fortune attached to the subject's not seeking to enjoy his revenues in his own family' shows how talents and virtue are nourished. 'It will be advantageous to cross the great stream:'—(the fifth line, representing the ruler,) is responded to by (the second, the central line of Khien, representing) Heaven.

image.zh_hant: 天在山中，大畜。君子以多識前言往行以畜其德。
image.zh_hans: 天在山中，大畜。君子以多识前言往行以畜其德。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and in the midst of it that (representing) heaven, form Ta Khu. The superior man, in accordance with this, stores largely in his memory the words and deeds of former men, to subserve the accumulation of his virtue.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject in a position of peril. It will be advantageous for him to stop his advance.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is in a position of peril; it will be advantageous for him to stop his advance:'—he should not rashly expose himself to calamity.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows a carriage with the strap under it removed.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: '(He is as) a carriage from which the strap under it has been removed:'—being in the central position, he will incur no blame.

text.zh_hant: 良馬逐，利艱貞，曰閑輿衛，利有攸往。
text.zh_hans: 良马逐，利艰贞，曰闲舆卫，利有攸往。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject urging his way with good horses. It will be advantageous for him to realise the difficulty (of his course), and to be firm and correct, exercising himself daily in his charioteering and methods of defence; then there will be advantage in whatever direction he may advance.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There will be advantage in whatever direction he may advance:'—(the subject of) the topmost line is of the same mind with him.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows the young bull, (and yet) having the piece of wood over his horns. There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The great good fortune indicated by the fourth line, divided,' shows that there is occasion for joy.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows the teeth of a castrated hog. There will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune indicated by the fifth line, divided,' shows that there is occasion for congratulation.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows its subject (as) in command of the firmament of heaven. There will be progress.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'In command of the firmament of heaven:'—the way is grandly open for movement.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: I indicates that with firm correctness there will be good fortune (in what is denoted by it). We must look at what we are seeking to nourish, and by the exercise of our thoughts seek for the proper aliment.

tuan.zh_hant: 頤貞吉，養正則吉也。觀頤、觀其所養也，自求口實、觀其自養也。天地養萬物，聖人養賢以及萬民，頤之時大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 颐贞吉，养正则吉也。观颐、观其所养也，自求口实、观其自养也。天地养万物，圣人养贤以及万民，颐之时大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: 'I indicates that with firm correctness there will be good fortune:'—when the nourishing is correct, there will be good fortune. 'We must look at what we are seeking to nourish:'—we must look at those whom we wish to nourish. 'We must by the exercise of our thoughts seek the proper aliment:'—we must look to our own nourishing of ourselves. Heaven and earth nourish all things. The sages nourish men of talents and virtue, by them to reach to the myriads of the people. Great is (the work intended by this) nourishing in its time! What will not a high and good purpose, supported by the greatest strength, be able to do?

image.zh_hant: 山下有雷，頤。君子以慎言語、節飲食。
image.zh_hans: 山下有雷，颐。君子以慎言语、节饮食。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a mountain and under it that for thunder form I. The superior man, in accordance with this, (enjoins) watchfulness over our words, and the temperate regulation of our eating and drinking.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, (seems to be thus addressed), 'You leave your efficacious tortoise, and look at me till your lower jaw hangs down.' There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'You look at me till your (lower) jaw hangs down:'—(the subject of the line) is thus shown unfit to be thought noble.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one looking downwards for nourishment, which is contrary to what is proper; or seeking it from the height (above), advance towards which will lead to evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The evil of advance by the subject of the second line, divided,' is owing to his leaving in his movements his proper associates.

text.zh_hant: 拂頤貞、凶，十年勿用，无攸利。
text.zh_hans: 拂颐贞、凶，十年勿用，无攸利。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows one acting contrary to the method of nourishing. However firm he may be, there will be evil. For ten years let him not take any action, (for) it will not be in any way advantageous.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'For ten years let him not take any action:'—his course is greatly opposed (to what is right).

text.zh_hant: 顛頤，吉。虎視眈眈，其欲逐逐，无咎。
text.zh_hans: 颠颐，吉。虎视眈眈，其欲逐逐，无咎。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows one looking downwards for (the power to) nourish. There will be good fortune. Looking with a tiger's downward unwavering glare, and with his desire that impels him to spring after spring, he will fall into no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune attached to looking downwards for (the power to) nourish,' shows how brilliant will be the diffusion (of that power) from (the subject of the line's) superior position.

text.zh_hant: 拂經，居貞、吉，不可涉大川。
text.zh_hans: 拂经，居贞、吉，不可涉大川。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows one acting contrary to what is regular and proper; but if he abide in firmness, there will be good fortune. He should not, (however, try to) cross the great stream.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune from abiding in firmness' is due to the docility (of the subject of the line) in following (the subject of the line) above.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows him from whom comes the nourishing. His position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune, notwithstanding the peril of his position, of him from whom comes the nourishing,' affords great cause for congratulation.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Ta Kwo suggests to us a beam that is weak. There will be advantage in moving (under its conditions) in any direction whatever; there will be success.

tuan.zh_hant: 大過、大者過也。棟橈、本末弱也。剛過而中，巽而說，行。利有攸往乃亨。大過之時大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 大过、大者过也。栋桡、本末弱也。刚过而中，巽而说，行。利有攸往乃亨。大过之时大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: Ta Kwo shows the great ones (= the undivided lines) in excess. In 'the beam that is weak' we see weakness both in the lowest and the topmost (lines). The strong lines are in excess, but (two of them) are in the central positions. The action (of the hexagram is represented by the symbols of) flexibility and satisfaction. (Hence it is said), 'There will be advantage in moving in any direction whatever; yea, there will be success.' Great indeed is (the work to be done in) this very extraordinary time.

image.zh_hant: 澤滅木，大過。君子以獨立不懼，遯世无悶。
image.zh_hans: 泽灭木，大过。君子以独立不惧，遯世无闷。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) trees hidden beneath that for the waters of a marsh forms Ta Kwo. The superior man, in accordance with this, stands up alone and has no fear, and keeps retired from the world without regret.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows one placing mats of the white mao grass under things set on the ground. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He places mats of the white mao grass under things set on the ground:'—he feels his weakness and his being in the lowest place, (and uses extraordinary care).

text.zh_hant: 枯楊生稊，老夫得其女妻，无不利。
text.zh_hans: 枯杨生稊，老夫得其女妻，无不利。
text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows a decayed willow producing shoots, or an old husband in possession of his young wife. There will be advantage in every way.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'An old husband and a young wife:'—such association is extraordinary.

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows a beam that is weak. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 棟橈之凶、不可以有輔也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 栋桡之凶、不可以有辅也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The evil connected with the beam that is weak' arises from this, that no help can be given (to the condition thus represented).

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows a beam curving upwards. There will be good fortune. If (the subject of it) looks for other (help but that of line one), there will be cause for regret.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune connected with the beam curving upwards' arises from this, that it does not bend towards what is below.

text.zh_hant: 枯楊生華，老婦得其士夫，无咎无譽。
text.zh_hans: 枯杨生华，老妇得其士夫，无咎无誉。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows a decayed willow producing flowers, or an old wife in possession of her young husband. There will be occasion neither for blame nor for praise.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 枯楊生華、何可久也，老婦士夫、亦可醜也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 枯杨生华、何可久也，老妇士夫、亦可丑也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A decayed willow produces flowers:'—but how can this secure its long continuance? 'An old wife and a young husband:'—this also is a thing to be ashamed of.

text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject with extraordinary (boldness) wading through a stream, till the water hides the crown of his head. There will be evil, but no ground for blame.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Evil follows wading with (extraordinary) boldness (through the stream):'—but (the act) affords no ground for blame.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 習坎，有孚，維心、亨。行有尚。
judgment.zh_hans: 习坎，有孚，维心、亨。行有尚。
judgment.en_legge: Khan, here repeated, shows the possession of sincerity, through which the mind is penetrating. Action (in accordance with this) will be of high value.

tuan.zh_hant: 習坎、重險也。水流而不盈。行險而不失其信。維心亨、乃以剛中也，行有尚、往有功也，天險、不可升也，地險、山川丘陵也。王公設險以守其國。險之時用大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 习坎、重险也。水流而不盈。行险而不失其信。维心亨、乃以刚中也，行有尚、往有功也，天险、不可升也，地险、山川丘陵也。王公设险以守其国。险之时用大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: Khan repeated shows us one defile succeeding another. This is the nature of water;—it flows on, without accumulating its volume (so as to overflow); it pursues its way through a dangerous defile, without losing its true (nature). That 'the mind is penetrating' is indicated by the strong (line) in the centre. That 'action (in accordance with this) will be of high value' tells us that advance will be followed by achievement. The dangerous (height) of heaven cannot be ascended; the difficult places of the earth are moun-tains, rivers, hills, and mounds. Kings and princes arrange, by means of such strengths, to maintain their territories. Great indeed is the use of (what is here) taught about seasons of peril.

image.zh_hant: 水洊至，習坎。君子以常德行、習教事。
image.zh_hans: 水洊至，习坎。君子以常德行、习教事。
image.en_legge: (The representation of) water flowing on continuously forms the repeated Khan, The superior man, in accordance with this, maintains constantly the virtue (of his heart) and (the integrity of) his conduct, and practises the business of instruction.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows its subject in the double defile, and (yet) entering a cavern within it. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'In the double defile, he enters a cavern within it:'—he has missed his (proper) way, and there will be evil.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject in all the peril of the defile. He will, however, get a little (of the deliverance) that he seeks.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He will get a little (of the deliverance) that he seeks:'—he will not yet escape from his environed position.

text.zh_hant: 來之坎坎，險且枕，入于坎窞，勿用。
text.zh_hans: 来之坎坎，险且枕，入于坎窞，勿用。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject, whether he comes or goes (=descends or ascends), confronted by a defile. All is peril to him and unrest. (His endeavours) will lead him into the cavern of the pit. There should be no action (in such a case).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Whether he comes or goes, he is confronted by a defile:'—he will never (in such circumstances) achieve any success.

text.zh_hant: 樽酒、簋貳、用缶，納約自牖，終无咎。
text.zh_hans: 樽酒、簋贰、用缶，纳约自牖，终无咎。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject (at a feast), with (simply) a bottle of spirits, and a subsidiary basket of rice, while (the cups and bowls) are (only) of earthenware. He introduces his important lessons (as his ruler's) intelligence admits. There will in the end be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: '(Nothing but) a bottle of spirits and a subsidiary basket of rice:'—(these describe) the meeting at this point of (those who are represented by) the strong and weak lines.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows the water of the defile not yet full, (so that it might flow away); but order will (soon) be brought about. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The water in the defile is not full (so as to flow away):'—(the virtue indicated by) the central situation is not yet (sufficiently) great.

text.zh_hant: 係用徽纆，寘于叢棘，三歲不得，凶。
text.zh_hans: 系用徽𬙊，寘于丛棘，三岁不得，凶。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject bound with cords of three strands or two strands, and placed in the thicket of thorns. But in three years he does not learn the course for him to pursue. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The sixth line, divided, shows its subject missing his (proper) course:'—'there will be evil for three years.'

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Li indicates that, (in regard to what it denotes), it will be advantageous to be firm and correct, and that thus there will be free course and success. Let (its subject) also nourish (a docility like that of) the cow, and there will be good fortune.

tuan.zh_hant: 離、麗也。日月麗乎天，百穀草木麗乎土。重明以麗乎正，乃化成天下。柔麗乎中正，故亨，是以畜牝牛吉也。
tuan.zh_hans: 离、丽也。日月丽乎天，百谷草木丽乎土。重明以丽乎正，乃化成天下。柔丽乎中正，故亨，是以畜牝牛吉也。
tuan.en_legge: Li means being attached to. The sun and moon have their place in the sky. All the grains, grass, and trees have their place on the earth. The double brightness (of the two trigrams) adheres to what is correct, and the result is the transforming and perfecting all under the sky. The weak (second line) occupies the middle and correct position, and gives the indication of 'a free and successful course;' and, moreover, 'nourishing (docility like that of) the cow' will lead to good fortune.

image.zh_hant: 明兩、作離。大人以繼明照于四方。
image.zh_hans: 明两、作离。大人以继明照于四方。
image.en_legge: (The trigram for) brightness, repeated, forms Li. The great man, in accordance with this, cultivates more and more his brilliant (virtue), and diffuses its brightness over the four quarters (of the land).

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows one ready to move with confused steps. But he treads at the same time reverently, and there will be no mistake.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The reverent attention directed to his confused steps' is the way by which error is avoided.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject in his place in yellow. There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The great good fortune (from the subject of the second line) occupying his place in yellow' is owing to his holding the course of the due mean.

text.zh_hant: 日昃之離，不鼓缶而歌，則大耋之嗟，凶。
text.zh_hans: 日昃之离，不鼓缶而歌，则大耋之嗟，凶。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject in a position like that of the declining sun. Instead of playing on his instrument of earthenware, and singing to it, he utters the groans of an old man of eighty. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A position like that of the declining sun:'—how can it continue long?

text.zh_hant: 突如、其來如，焚如，死如，棄如。
text.zh_hans: 突如、其来如，焚如，死如，弃如。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows the manner of its subject's coming. How abrupt it is, as with fire, with death, to be rejected (by all)!

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'How abrupt is the manner of his coming!'—none can bear with him.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows its subject as one with tears flowing in torrents, and groaning in sorrow. There will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune attached to the fifth line, divided,' is due to its occupying the place of a king or a prince.

text.zh_hant: 王用出征，有嘉折首，獲匪其醜，无咎。
text.zh_hans: 王用出征，有嘉折首，获匪其丑，无咎。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows the king employing its subject in his punitive expeditions. Achieving admirable (merit), he breaks (only) the chiefs (of the rebels). Where his prisoners were not their associates, he does not punish. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The king employs him in his punitive expeditions:'—the object is to bring the regions to a correct state.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Hsien indicates that, (on the fulfilment of the conditions implied in it), there will be free course and success. Its advantageousness will depend on the being firm and correct, (as) in marrying a young lady. There will be good fortune.

tuan.zh_hant: 咸、感也。柔上而剛下，二氣感應以相與，止而說，男下女，是以亨利貞、取女吉也。天地感而萬物化生，聖人感人心而天下和平。觀其所感而天地萬物之情可見矣。
tuan.zh_hans: 咸、感也。柔上而刚下，二气感应以相与，止而说，男下女，是以亨利贞、取女吉也。天地感而万物化生，圣人感人心而天下和平。观其所感而天地万物之情可见矣。
tuan.en_legge: Hsien is here used in the sense of Kan, meaning (mutually) influencing. The weak (trigram) above, and the strong one below; their two influences moving and responding to each other, and thereby forming a union; the repression (of the one) and the satisfaction (of the other); (with their relative position), where the male is placed below the female:—all these things convey the notion of 'a free and successful course (on the fulfilment of the conditions), while the advantage will depend on being firm and correct, as in marrying a young lady, and there will be good fortune.' Heaven and earth exert their influences, and there ensue the transformation and production of all things. The sages influence the minds of men, and the result is harmony and peace all under the sky. If we look at (the method and issues) of those influences, the true character of heaven and earth and of all things can be seen.

image.zh_hant: 山上有澤，咸。君子以虛受人。
image.zh_hans: 山上有泽，咸。君子以虚受人。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a mountain and above it that for (the waters of) a marsh form Hsien. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps his mind free from pre-occupation, and open to receive (the influences of) others.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows one moving his great toes.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He moves his great toe:'—his mind is set on what is beyond (himself).

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows one moving the calves of his leg. There will be evil. If he abide (quiet in his place), there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: Though 'there would be evil; yet, if he abide (quiet) in his place, there will be good fortune:'—through compliance (with the circumstances of his condition and place) there will be no injury.

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows one moving his thighs, and keeping close hold of those whom he follows. Going forward (in this way) will cause regret.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 咸其股、亦不處也，志在隨人、所執下也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 咸其股、亦不处也，志在随人、所执下也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He moves his thighs:'—he still does not (want to) rest in his place. His will is set on 'following others:'—what he holds in his grasp is low.

text.zh_hant: 貞吉。悔亡。憧憧往來，朋從爾思。
text.zh_hans: 贞吉。悔亡。憧憧往来，朋从尔思。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows that firm correctness which will lead to good fortune, and prevent all occasion for repentance. If its subject be unsettled in his movements, (only) his friends will follow his purpose.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 貞吉悔亡、未感害也，憧憧往來、未光大也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 贞吉悔亡、未感害也，憧憧往来、未光大也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Firm correctness will lead to good fortune, and prevent all occasion for repentance:'—there has not yet been any harm from (a selfish wish to) influence. 'He is unsettled in his movements:'—(his power to influence) is not yet either brilliant or great.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows one moving the flesh along the spine above the heart. There will be no occasion for repentance.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He (tries to) move the flesh along the spine above the heart:'—his aim is trivial.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows one moving his jaws and tongue.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He moves his jaws and tongue:'—he (only) talks with loquacious mouth.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Hang indicates successful progress and no error (in what it denotes). But the advantage will come from being firm and correct; and movement in any direction whatever will be advantageous.

tuan.zh_hant: 《恆》、久也。剛上而柔下。雷風相與。巽而動，剛柔皆應，《恆》。恆亨无咎利貞、久於其道也。天地之道恆久而不已也。利有攸往、終則有始也。日月得天而能久照，四時變化而能久成。聖人久於其道而天下化成。觀其所恆而天地萬物之情可見矣。
tuan.zh_hans: 《恒》、久也。刚上而柔下。雷风相与。巽而动，刚柔皆应，《恒》。恒亨无咎利贞、久于其道也。天地之道恒久而不已也。利有攸往、终则有始也。日月得天而能久照，四时变化而能久成。圣人久于其道而天下化成。观其所恒而天地万物之情可见矣。
tuan.en_legge: Hang denotes long continuance. The strong (trigram) is above, and the weak one below; (they are the symbols of) thunder and wind, which are in mutual communication; (they have the qualities of) docility and motive force; their strong and weak (lines) all respond, each to the other:—these things are all found in Hang. (When it is said that) 'Hang indicates successful progress and no error (in what it denotes); but the advantage will come from being firm and correct,' this indicates that there must be long continuance in its way of operation. The way of heaven and earth is to be long continued in their operation without stopping. (When it is said that) 'Movement in any direction whatever will be advantageous,' this implies that when (the moving power) is spent, it will begin again. The sun and moon, realising in themselves (the course of Heaven), can perpetuate their shining. The four seasons, by their changing and transforming, can perpetuate their production (of things). The sages persevere long in their course, and all under the sky are transformed and perfect. When we look at what they continue doing long, the natural tendencies of heaven, earth, and all things can be seen.

image.zh_hant: 雷風《恆》。君子以立不易方。
image.zh_hans: 雷风《恒》。君子以立不易方。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for wind form Hang. The superior man, in accordance with this, stands firm, and does not change his method (of operation).

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows its subject deeply (desirous) of long continuance. Even with firm Neither can the thighs move of themselves. The attempt to correctness there will be evil; there will be no advantage in any way.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The evil attached to the deep desire for long continuance (in the subject of the first line)' arises from the deep seeking for it at the commencement (of things).

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows all occasion for repentance disappearing.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'All occasion for repentance on the part of the subject of the second line, undivided, disappears:'—he can abide long in the due mean.

text.zh_hant: 不恆其德，或承之羞，貞吝。
text.zh_hans: 不恒其德，或承之羞，贞吝。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows one who does not continuously maintain his virtue. There are those who will impute this to him as a disgrace. However firm he may be, there will be ground for regret.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He does not continuously maintain his virtue:'—nowhere will he be borne with.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows a field where there is no game.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: (Going) for long to what is not his proper place, how can he get game?

text.zh_hant: 恆其德、貞，婦人吉，夫子凶。
text.zh_hans: 恒其德、贞，妇人吉，夫子凶。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows its subject continuously maintaining the virtue indicated by it. In a wife this will be fortunate; in a husband, evil.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 婦人貞吉、從一而終也。夫子制義、從婦凶也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 妇人贞吉、从一而终也。夫子制义、从妇凶也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Such firm correctness in a wife will be fortunate:'—it is hers to the end of life to follow with an unchanged mind. The husband must decide what is right, and lay down the rule accordingly:—for him to follow (like) a wife is evil.

text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject exciting himself to long continuance. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The subject of the topmost line is exciting himself to long continuance:'—far will he be from achieving merit.
