judgment.en_legge: Thun indicates successful progress (in its circumstances). To a small extent it will (still) be advantageous to be firm and correct.

tuan.zh_hant: 遯亨，遯而亨也。剛當位而應，與時行也。小利貞、浸而長也。遯之時義大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 遯亨，遯而亨也。刚当位而应，与时行也。小利贞、浸而长也。遯之时义大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: 'Thun indicates successful progress:'—that is, in the very retiring which Thun denotes there is such progress. The strong (line) is in the ruling place, (the fifth), and is properly responded to (by the second line). The action takes place according to (the requirement of) the time. 'To a small extent it will (still) be advantageous to be firm and correct:'—(the small men) are gradually encroaching and advancing. Great indeed is the significance of (what is required to be done in) the time that necessitates retiring.

image.zh_hant: 天下有山，遯。君子以遠小人，不惡而嚴。
image.zh_hans: 天下有山，遯。君子以远小人，不恶而严。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) the sky and below it that for a mountain form Thun. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps small men at a distance, not by showing that he hates them, but by his own dignified gravity.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows a retiring tail. The position is perilous. No movement in any direction should be made.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: There is 'the perilousness of the position shown by the retiring tail:'—but if 'no movement' be made, what disaster can there be?

text.zh_hant: 執之用黃牛之革，莫之勝、說。
text.zh_hans: 执之用黄牛之革，莫之胜、说。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject holding (his purpose) fast as if by a (thong made from the) hide of a yellow ox, which cannot be broken.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He holds it as by (a thong from the hide of) a yellow ox:'—his purpose is firm.

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows one retiring but bound,—to his distress and peril. (If he were to deal with his binders as in) nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for him.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 係遯之厲、有疾憊也，畜臣妾吉、不可大事也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 系遯之厉、有疾惫也，畜臣妾吉、不可大事也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The peril connected with the case of one retiring, though bound,' is due to the (consequent) distress and exhaustion. 'If he were (to deal as in) nourishing a servant or concubine, it would be fortunate for him:'—but a great affair cannot be dealt with in this way.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject retiring notwithstanding his likings. In a superior man this will lead to good fortune; a small man cannot attain to this.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A superior man retires notwithstanding his likings; a small man cannot attain to this.'

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject retiring in an admirable way. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He retires in an admirable way, and with firm correctness there will be good fortune:'—this is due to the rectitude of his purpose.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows its subject retiring in a noble way. It will be advantageous in every respect.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He retires in a noble way, and his doing so will be advantageous in every respect:'—he who does so has no doubts about his course.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Ta Kwang indicates that (under the conditions which it symbolises) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.

tuan.zh_hant: 大壯、大者壯也。剛以動，故壯。大壯利貞，大者、正也。正大而天地之情可見矣。
tuan.zh_hans: 大壮、大者壮也。刚以动，故壮。大壮利贞，大者、正也。正大而天地之情可见矣。
tuan.en_legge: In Ta Kwang we see that which is great becoming strong. We have the (trigram) denoting strength directing that which denotes movement, and hence (the whole) is expressive of vigour. 'Ta Kwang indicates that it will be advantageous to be firm and correct:'—that which is great (should be) correct. Given correctness and greatness (in their highest degree), and the character and tendencies of heaven and earth can be seen.

image.zh_hant: 雷在天上，大壯。君子以非禮弗履。
image.zh_hans: 雷在天上，大壮。君子以非礼弗履。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) heaven and above it that for thunder form Ta A wang. The superior man, in accordance with this, does not take a step which is not according to propriety.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject manifesting his strength in his toes. But advance will lead to evil,—most certainly.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He manifests his vigour in his toes:'—this will certainly lead to exhaustion.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows that with firm correctness there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The second line, undivided, shows that with firm correctness there will be good fortune:'—this is due to its being in the centre, (and its subject exemplifying the due mean).

text.zh_hant: 小人用壯，君子用罔，貞厲。羝羊觸藩，羸其角。
text.zh_hans: 小人用壮，君子用罔，贞厉。羝羊触藩，羸其角。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows, in the case of a small man, one using all his strength; and in the case of a superior man, one whose rule is not to do so. Even with firm correctness the position would be perilous. (The exercise of strength in it might be compared to the case of) a ram butting against a fence, and getting his horns entangled.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The small man uses all his strength; in the case of the superior man it is his rule not to do so.'

text.zh_hant: 貞吉，悔亡。藩決不羸，壯于大輿之輹。
text.zh_hans: 贞吉，悔亡。藩决不羸，壮于大舆之輹。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows (a case in which) firm correctness leads to good fortune, and occasion for repentance disappears. (We see) the fence opened without the horns being entangled. The strength is like that in the wheel-spokes of a large waggon.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The fence is opened and the horns are not entangled:'—(the subject of the line) still advances.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows one who loses his ram(-like strength) in the ease of his position, (But) there will be no occasion for repentance.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He loses his ram and hardly perceives it:'—he is not in his appropriate place.

text.zh_hant: 羝羊觸藩，不能退，不能遂，无攸利，艱則吉。
text.zh_hans: 羝羊触藩，不能退，不能遂，无攸利，艰则吉。
text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows (one who may be compared to) the ram butting against the fence, and unable either to retreat, or to advance as he would fain do. There will not be advantage in any respect; but if he realise the difficulty (of his position), there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 不能退、不能遂、不詳也，艱則吉、咎不長也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 不能退、不能遂、不详也，艰则吉、咎不长也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is unable either to retreat or to advance:'—this is owing to his want of care. 'If he realise the difficulty (of his position), there will be good fortune:'—his error will not be prolonged.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接。
judgment.zh_hans: 康侯用锡马蕃庶，昼日三接。
judgment.en_legge: In Zin we see a prince who secures the tranquillity (of the people) presented on that account with numerous horses (by the king), and three times in a day received at interviews.

tuan.zh_hant: 晉、進也。明出地上。順而麗乎大明，柔進而上行，是以康侯用錫馬蕃庶晝日三接也。
tuan.zh_hans: 晋、进也。明出地上。顺而丽乎大明，柔进而上行，是以康侯用锡马蕃庶昼日三接也。
tuan.en_legge: Zin denotes advancing. (In Zin we have) the bright (sun) appearing above the earth; (the symbol of) docile submission cleaving to that of the Great brightness; and the weak line advanced and moving above:—all these things give us the idea of 'a prince who secures the tranquillity (of the people), presented on that account with numerous horses (by the king), and three times in a day received at interviews.'

image.zh_hant: 明出地上，晉。君子以自昭明德。
image.zh_hans: 明出地上，晋。君子以自昭明德。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for the bright (sun) coming forth above it form Zin. The superior man, according to this, gives himself to make more brilliant his bright virtue.

text.zh_hant: 晉如摧如，貞吉。罔孚，裕无咎。
text.zh_hans: 晋如摧如，贞吉。罔孚，裕无咎。
text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows one wishing to advance, and (at the same time) kept back. Let him be firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. If trust be not reposed in him, let him maintain a large and generous mind, and there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 晉如摧如、獨行正也，裕无咎、未受命也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 晋如摧如、独行正也，裕无咎、未受命也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He appears wishing to advance, but (at the same time) being kept back:'—all-alone he pursues the correct course. 'Let him maintain a large and generous mind, and there will be no error:'—he has not yet received an official charge.

text.zh_hant: 晉如，愁如，貞吉。受茲介福于其王母。
text.zh_hans: 晋如，愁如，贞吉。受兹介福于其王母。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, and yet of being sorrowful. If he be firm and correct, there will be good fortune. He will receive this great blessing from his grandmother.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He will receive this great blessing:'—for he is in the central place and the correct position for him.

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject trusted by all (around him). All occasion for repentance will disappear.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'All (around) trust him:'—their (common) aim is to move upwards and act.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject with the appearance of advancing, but like a marmot. However firm and correct he may be, the position is one of peril.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: '(He advances like) a marmot. However firm and correct he may be, his position is one of peril:'—his place is not that appropriate for him.

text.zh_hant: 悔亡，失得勿恤。往吉，无不利。
text.zh_hans: 悔亡，失得勿恤。往吉，无不利。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows how all occasion for repentance disappears (from its subject). (But) let him not concern himself about whether he shall fail or succeed. To advance will be fortunate, and in every way advantageous.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Let him not concern himself whether he fails or succeeds:'—his movement in advance will afford ground for congratulation.

text.zh_hant: 晉其角，維用伐邑，厲吉，无咎，貞吝。
text.zh_hans: 晋其角，维用伐邑，厉吉，无咎，贞吝。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows one advancing his horns. But he only uses them to punish the (rebellious people of his own) city. The position is perilous, but there will be good fortune. (Yet) however firm and correct he may be, there will be occasion for regret.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He uses his horns only to punish (the rebellious people of) his city:'—his course of procedure is not yet brilliant.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Ming I indicates that (in the circumstances which it denotes) it will be advantageous to realise the difficulty (of the position), and maintain firm correctness.

tuan.zh_hant: 明入地中，明夷。內文明而外柔順，以蒙大難，文王以之。利艱貞、晦其明也，內難而能正其志，箕子以之。
tuan.zh_hans: 明入地中，明夷。内文明而外柔顺，以蒙大难，文王以之。利艰贞、晦其明也，内难而能正其志，箕子以之。
tuan.en_legge: (The symbol of) the Earth and that of Brightness entering into the midst of it give the idea of Ming I (Brightness wounded or obscured). The inner (trigram) denotes being accomplished and bright; the outer, being pliant and submissive. The case of king Wan was that of one who with these qualities was yet involved in great difficulties. 'It will be advantageous to realise the difficulty (of the position), and maintain firm correctness:'—that is, (the individual concerned) should obscure his brightness. The case of the count of Ki was that of one who, amidst the difficulties of his House, was able (thus) to maintain his aim and mind correct.

image.zh_hant: 明入地中，明夷。君子以莅眾用晦而明。
image.zh_hans: 明入地中，明夷。君子以莅众用晦而明。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) the earth and that for the bright (sun) entering within it form Ming I. The superior man, in accordance with this, conducts his management of men;—he shows his intelligence by keeping it obscured.

text.zh_hant: 明夷于飛，垂其翼。君子于行，三日不食。有攸往，主人有言。
text.zh_hans: 明夷于飞，垂其翼。君子于行，三日不食。有攸往，主人有言。
text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its: subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming ], flying, but with drooping wings. When the superior man (is revolving) his going away, he may be for three days without eating. Wherever he goes, the people there may speak (derisively of him).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The superior man (is revolving his) going away:'—(in such a case) he feels it right not to eat.

text.zh_hant: 明夷、夷于左股，用拯馬、壯吉。
text.zh_hans: 明夷、夷于左股，用拯马、壮吉。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming I, wounded in the left thigh. He saves himself by the strength of a (swift) horse; and is fortunate.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune of (the subject of) the second line, divided,' is due to the proper fashion of his acting according to his circumstances.

text.zh_hant: 明夷于南狩，得其大首，不可疾貞。
text.zh_hans: 明夷于南狩，得其大首，不可疾贞。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject, (in the condition indicated by) Ming I, hunting in the south, and taking the great chief (of the darkness). He should not be eager to make (all) correct (at once).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: With the aim represented by 'hunting in the south' a great achievement is accomplished.

text.zh_hant: 入于左腹，獲明夷之心于出門庭。
text.zh_hans: 入于左腹，获明夷之心于出门庭。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject (just) entered into the left side of the belly (of the dark land). (But) he is able to carry out the mind appropriate (in the condition indicated by) Ming I, quitting the gate and courtyard (of the lord of darkness).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He has (just) entered into the left side of the belly (of the dark land):'—he is still able to carry out the idea in his (inner) mind.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows how the count of Ki fulfilled the condition indicated by Ming I. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'With the firm correctness of the count of Ki,' his brightness could not be (quite) extinguished.

text.zh_hant: 不明、晦。初登于天，後入于地。
text.zh_hans: 不明、晦。初登于天，后入于地。
text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows the case where there is no light, but (only) obscurity. (Its subject) had at first ascended to (the top of) the sky; his future shall be to go into the earth.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 初登于天、照四國也，後入于地、失則也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 初登于天、照四国也，后入于地、失则也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He had at first ascended to (the top of) the sky:'—he might have enlightened the four quarters of the kingdom. 'His future shall be to go into the earth:'—he has failed to fulfil the model (of a ruler).

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: For (the realisation of what is taught in) Kia Zan, (or for the regulation of the family), what is most advantageous is that the wife be firm and correct.

tuan.zh_hant: 家人，女正位乎內，男正位乎外。男女正，天地之大義也。家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟、夫夫、婦婦而家道正，正家而天下定矣。
tuan.zh_hans: 家人，女正位乎内，男正位乎外。男女正，天地之大义也。家人有严君焉，父母之谓也。父父、子子、兄兄、弟弟、夫夫、妇妇而家道正，正家而天下定矣。
tuan.en_legge: In Kia Zan the wife has her correct place in the inner (trigram), and the man his correct place in the outer. That man and woman occupy their correct places is the great righteousness shown (in the relation and positions of) heaven and earth. In Kia Zan we have the idea of an authoritative ruler;—that, namely, represented by the parental authority. Let the father be indeed father, and the son son; let the elder brother be indeed elder brother, and the younger brother younger brother; let the husband be indeed husband, and the wife wife:-—then will the family be in its normal state. Bring the family to that state, and all under heaven will be established.

image.zh_hant: 風自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恆。
image.zh_hans: 风自火出，家人。君子以言有物而行有恒。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) fire, and that for wind coming forth from it, form Kia Zan. The superior man, in accordance with this, orders his words according to (the truth of) things, and his conduct so that it is uniformly consistent.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject establishing restrictive regulations in his household. Occasion for repentance will disappear.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He establishes restrictive regulations in his household:'—(he does so), before any change has taken place in their wills.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject taking nothing on herself, but in her central place attending to the preparation of the food. Through her firm correctness there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune attached to the second line, divided,' is due to the docility (of its subject), operating with humility.

text.zh_hant: 家人嗃嗃，悔厲，吉；婦子嘻嘻，終吝。
text.zh_hans: 家人嗃嗃，悔厉，吉；妇子嘻嘻，终吝。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject (treating) the members of the household with stern severity. There will be occasion for repentance, there will be peril, (but) there will (also) be good fortune. If the wife and children were to be smirking and chattering, in the end there would be occasion for regret.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 家人嗃嗃、未失也，婦子嘻嘻、失家節也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 家人嗃嗃、未失也，妇子嘻嘻、失家节也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: When 'the members of the household are treated with stern severity,' there has been no (great) failure (in the regulation of the family). When 'wife and children are smirking and chattering,' the (proper) economy of the family has been lost.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject enriching the family. There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The family is enriched, and there is great good fortune:'—this is due to the docility (belonging to the subject of the line), and its being in its correct place.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows the influence of the king extending to his family. There need be no anxiety; there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The influence of the king extends to his family:'—the intercourse between them is that of mutual love.

text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject possessed of sincerity and arrayed in majesty. In the end there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune connected with the display of majesty' describes (the result of) the recovery of the true character.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Khwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.

tuan.zh_hant: 睽、火動而上，澤動而下。二女同居，其志不同行。說而麗乎明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛，是以小事吉。天地睽而其事同也。男女睽而其志通也。萬物睽而其事類也，睽之時用大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 睽、火动而上，泽动而下。二女同居，其志不同行。说而丽乎明，柔进而上行，得中而应乎刚，是以小事吉。天地睽而其事同也。男女睽而其志通也。万物睽而其事类也，睽之时用大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: In Khwei we have (the symbol of) Fire, which, when moved, tends upwards, and that of a Marsh, whose waters, when moved, tend downwards. We have (also the symbols of) two sisters living together, but whose wills do not move in the same direction. (We see how the inner trigram expressive of) harmonious satisfaction is attached to (the outer expressive of) bright intelligence; (we see) the weak line advanced and acting above, and how it occupies the central place, and is responded to by the strong (line below). These indications show that 'in small matters there will (still) be good fortune.' Heaven and earth are separate and apart, but the work which they do is the same. Male and female are separate and apart, but with a common will they seek the same object. There is diversity between the myriad classes of beings, but there is an analogy between their several operations. Great indeed are the phenomena and the results of this condition of disunion and separation.

image.zh_hant: 上火下澤，睽。君子以同而異。
image.zh_hans: 上火下泽，睽。君子以同而异。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) fire above, and that for (the waters of) a marsh below, form Khwei. The superior man, in accordance with this, where there is a general agreement, yet admits diversity.

text.zh_hant: 悔亡。喪馬，勿逐自復。見惡人无咎。
text.zh_hans: 悔亡。丧马，勿逐自复。见恶人无咎。
text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. He has lost his horses, but let him not seek for them;—they will return of themselves. Should he meet with bad men, he will not err (in communicating with them).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He meets with bad men (and communicates with them):'—(he does so), to avoid the evil of their condemnation.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject happening to meet with his lord in a bye-passage. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He happens to meet with his lord in a bye-passage:'—but he has not deviated (for this meeting) from the (proper) course.

text.zh_hant: 見輿曳，其牛掣，其人天且劓，无初有終。
text.zh_hans: 见舆曳，其牛掣，其人天且劓，无初有终。
text.en_legge: In the third line, divided, we see one whose carriage is dragged back, while the oxen in it are pushed back, and he is himself subjected to the shaving of his head and the cutting off of his nose. There is no good beginning, but there will be a good end.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 見輿曳、位不當也，无初有終、遇剛也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 见舆曳、位不当也，无初有终、遇刚也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'We see his carriage dragged back:'—this is indicated by the inappropriateness of the position (of the line). 'There is no (good) beginning, but there will be a (good) end:'—this arises from his meeting with the strong (subject of the topmost line).

text.zh_hant: 睽孤，遇元夫，交孚，厲无咎。
text.zh_hans: 睽孤，遇元夫，交孚，厉无咎。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (But) he meets with the good man (represented by the first line), and they blend their sincere desires together. The position is one of peril, but there will be no mistake.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'They blend their sincere desires together, and there will be no error:'—their (common) aim is carried into effect.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows that (to its subject) occasion for repentance will disappear. With his relative (and minister he unites closely and readily) as if he were biting through a piece of skin. When he goes forward (with this help), what error can there be?

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'With his hereditary minister (he unites closely and easily) as if he were biting through a piece of skin:'—his going forward will afford ground for congratulation.

text.zh_hant: 睽孤，見豕負塗，載鬼一車，先張之弧，後說之弧，匪寇，婚媾。往遇雨，則吉。
text.zh_hans: 睽孤，见豕负涂，载鬼一车，先张之弧，后说之弧，匪寇，婚媾。往遇雨，则吉。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject solitary amidst the (prevailing) disunion. (In the subject of the third line, he seems to) see a pig bearing on its back a load of mud, (or fancies) there is a carriage full of ghosts. He first bends his bow against him, and afterwards unbends it, (for he discovers) that he is not an assailant to injure, but a near relative. Going forward, he shall meet with (genial) rain, and there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune symbolised by meeting with (genial) rain' springs from the passing away of all doubts.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 利西南，不利東北。利見大人。貞吉。
judgment.zh_hans: 利西南，不利东北。利见大人。贞吉。
judgment.en_legge: In (the state indicated by) Kien advantage will be found in the south-west, and the contrary in the north-east. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man. (In these circumstances), with firmness and correctness, there will be good fortune.

tuan.zh_hant: 蹇、難也，險在前也。見險而能止，知矣哉！蹇、利西南，往得中也，不利東北、其道窮也，利見大人、往有功也，當位貞吉、以正邦也。蹇之時用大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 蹇、难也，险在前也。见险而能止，知矣哉！蹇、利西南，往得中也，不利东北、其道穷也，利见大人、往有功也，当位贞吉、以正邦也。蹇之时用大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: Kien denotes difficulty. There is (the trigram expressive of) perilousness in front. When one, seeing the peril, can arrest his steps (in accordance with the significance of the lower trigram), is he not wise? (The language of) Kien, that 'advantage will be found in the south-west,' refers to the (strong fifth line) advanced and in the central place. That 'there will be no advantage in the north-east,' intimates that the way (of dealing with the Kien state) is exhausted. That 'it will be advantageous to see the great man,' intimates that advance will lead to achievement. That the places (of the different lines after the first) are those appropriate to them indicates firm correctness and good fortune, with which the regions (of the kingdom) are brought to their normal state. Great indeed is the work to be done in the time of Kien!

image.zh_hant: 山上有水，蹇。君子以反身修德。
image.zh_hans: 山上有水，蹇。君子以反身修德。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a mountain, and above it that for water, form Kien. The superior man, in accordance with this, turns round (and examines) himself, and cultivates his virtue.

text.en_legge: From the first line, divided, we learn that advance (on the part of its subject) will lead to (greater) difficulties, while remaining stationary will afford ground for praise.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Advancing will conduct to (greater) difficulties, while remaining stationary will afford ground for praise:'—the proper course is to wait.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows the minister of the king struggling with difficulty on difficulty, and not with a view to his own advantage.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The minister of the king struggles with difficulty on difficulty:'—in the end no blame will be attached to him.

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and returns (to his former associates).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He advances, (but only) to (greater) difficulty; he remains stationary, and returns to his former associates:'—they, (represented in) the inner (trigram), rejoice in him.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject advancing, (but only) to (greater) difficulties. He remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'To advance will (only be to) encounter (greater) difficulties; he remains stationary, and unites (with the subject of the line above):'—that is in its proper place and has the solidity (due to it in that position).

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject struggling with the greatest difficulties, while friends are coming to help him.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He struggles with the greatest difficulties, while friends are coming (to help him):'—he is in the central position, and possesses the requisite virtue.

text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject going forward, (only to increase) the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will be (productive of) great (merit). There will be good fortune, and it will be advantageous to meet with the great man.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 往蹇來碩、志在內也，利見大人、以從貴也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 往蹇来硕、志在内也，利见大人、以从贵也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'To advance will (only) increase the difficulties, while his remaining stationary will (be productive of) great (merit):'—his aim is to assist the (subject of the line) inside of him. 'It will be advantageous to meet the great man:'—by his course he follows that noble (lord of the figure).

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 利西南。无所往，其來復吉。有攸往，夙吉。
judgment.zh_hans: 利西南。无所往，其来复吉。有攸往，夙吉。
judgment.en_legge: In (the state indicated by) Kieh advantage will be found in the south-west. If no (further) operations be called for, there will be good fortune in coming back (to the old conditions). If some operations be called for, there will be good fortune in the early conducting of them.

tuan.zh_hant: 解、險以動，動而免乎險，解。解利西南、往得眾也，其來復吉、乃得中也。有攸往夙吉、往有功也。天地解而雷雨作，雷雨作而百果草木皆甲坼。解之時大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 解、险以动，动而免乎险，解。解利西南、往得众也，其来复吉、乃得中也。有攸往夙吉、往有功也。天地解而雷雨作，雷雨作而百果草木皆甲坼。解之时大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: In Kieh we have (the trigram expressive of) peril going on to that expressive of movement. By movement there is an escape from the peril:—(this is the meaning of) Kieh. 'In (the state indicated by) Kieh, advantage will be found in the south-west:'—the movement (thus) intimated will win all. That 'there will be good fortune in coming back (to the old conditions)' shows that such action is that of the due medium. That 'if some operations be necessary, there will be good fortune in the early conducting of them' shows that such operations will be successful. When heaven and earth are freed (from the grasp of winter), we have thunder and rain. When these come, the buds of the plants and trees that produce the various fruits begin to burst. Great indeed are the phenomena in the time intimated by Kieh.

image.zh_hant: 雷雨作，解。君子以赦過宥罪。
image.zh_hans: 雷雨作，解。君子以赦过宥罪。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) thunder and that for rain, with these phenomena in a state of manifestation, form Kieh. The superior man, in accordance with this, forgives errors, and deals gently with crimes.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows that its subject will commit no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: The strong (fourth) line and the weak line here are in correlation:—we judge rightly in saying that 'its subject will commit no error.'

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject catch, in hunting, three foxes, and obtain the yellow (=golden) arrows. With firm correctness there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune springing from the firm correctness of the second line, undivided,' is due to its subject holding the due mean.

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows a porter with his burden, (yet) riding in a carriage. He will (only) tempt robbers to attack him. However firm and correct he may (try to) be, there will be cause for regret.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 負且乘、亦可醜也。自我致戎，又誰咎也？
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 负且乘、亦可丑也。自我致戎，又谁咎也？
xiao_xiang.en_legge: For 'a porter with his burden to be riding in a carriage' is a thing to be ashamed of. 'It is he himself that tempts the robbers to come:'—on whom besides can we lay the blame? (See Appendix III, i, 48.)

text.en_legge: (To the subject of) the fourth line, undivided, (it is said), 'Remove your toes. Friends will (then) come, between you and whom there will be mutual confidence.'

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Remove your toes:'—the places (of this line and of the third and first) are all inappropriate to them.

text.zh_hant: 君子維有解，吉，有孚于小人。
text.zh_hans: 君子维有解，吉，有孚于小人。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows (its subject), the superior man (=the ruler), executing his function of removing (whatever is injurious to the idea of the hexagram), in which case there will be good fortune, and confidence in him will be shown even by the small men.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: When 'the superior man executes his function of removing (whatever is injurious to the idea of the hexagram),' small men will of themselves retire.

text.zh_hant: 公用射隼于高墉之上，獲之，无不利。
text.zh_hans: 公用射隼于高墉之上，获之，无不利。
text.en_legge: In the sixth line, divided, we see a feudal prince (with his bow) shooting at a falcon on the top of a high wall, and hitting it. (The effect of his action) will be in every way advantageous.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A prince with his bow shoots a falcon:'—thus he removes (the promoters of) rebellion.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 有孚，元吉，无咎可貞。利有攸往。曷之用，二簋可用享。
judgment.zh_hans: 有孚，元吉，无咎可贞。利有攸往。曷之用，二簋可用享。
judgment.en_legge: In (what is denoted by) Sun, if there be sincerity (in him who employs it), there will be great good fortune:—freedom from error; firmness and correctness that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that shall be made. In what shall this (sincerity in the exercise of Sun) be employed? (Even) in sacrifice two baskets of grain, (though there be nothing else), may be presented.

tuan.zh_hant: 損、損下益上，其道上行。損而有孚，元吉、无咎、可貞、利有攸往、曷之用二簋、可用享，二簋應有時。損剛益柔有時，損益盈虛，與時偕行。
tuan.zh_hans: 损、损下益上，其道上行。损而有孚，元吉、无咎、可贞、利有攸往、曷之用二簋、可用享，二簋应有时。损刚益柔有时，损益盈虚，与时偕行。
tuan.en_legge: In Sun (we see) the lower (trigram) diminished, and the upper added to. (But) the method (of action) implied in this operates also above (or, mounts upwards (also) and operates). 'If there be sincerity in this method of diminution, there will be great good fortune; freedom from error; firmness and correctness that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that shall be made. In what shall this (sincerity in the exercise of Sun) be employed? (Even) in sacrifice, two baskets of grain, (though there be nothing else), may be presented:'—for these two baskets there ought to be the fitting time. There is a time when the strong should be diminished, and the weak should be strengthened. Diminution and increase, overflowing and emptiness:—these take place in harmony with the conditions of the time.

image.zh_hant: 山下有澤，損。君子以懲忿窒欲。
image.zh_hans: 山下有泽，损。君子以惩忿窒欲。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a mountain and beneath it that for the waters of a marsh form Sun. The superior man, in accordance with this, restrains his wrath and represses his desires.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject suspending his own affairs, and hurrying away (to help the subject of the fourth line). He will commit no error, but let him consider how far he should contribute of what is his (for the other).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He suspends his own affairs and hurries away (to help the subject of the fourth line):'—the (subject of that) upper (line) mingles his wishes with his.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject to maintain a firm correctness, and that action on his part will be evil. He can give increase (to his correlate) without taking from himself.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'It will be advantageous for (the subject of) the second line, undivided, to maintain his firm correctness:'—his central position gives its character to his aim.

text.zh_hant: 三人行則損一人，一人行則得其友。
text.zh_hans: 三人行则损一人，一人行则得其友。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows how of three men walking together, the number is diminished by one; and how one, walking, finds his friend.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'One man, walking,' (finds his friend):—when three are together, doubts rise among them.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject diminishing the ailment under which he labours by making (the subject of the first line) hasten (to his help), and make him glad. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He diminishes the ailment under which he labours:'—this is matter for joy.

text.zh_hant: 或益之十朋之龜，弗克違，元吉。
text.zh_hans: 或益之十朋之龟，弗克违，元吉。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows parties adding to (the stores of) its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells, and accepting no refusal. There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The great good fortune attached to the fifth line, divided,' is due to the blessing from above.

text.zh_hant: 弗損，益之，无咎，貞吉，利有攸往，得臣无家。
text.zh_hans: 弗损，益之，无咎，贞吉，利有攸往，得臣无家。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, undivided, shows its subject giving increase to others without taking from himself. There will be no error. With firm correctness there will be good fortune. There will be advantage in every movement that shall be made. He will find ministers more than can be counted by their clans.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He gives increase to others without taking from what is his own:'—he obtains his wish on a grand scale.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Yi indicates that (in the state which it denotes) there will be advantage in every movement which shall be undertaken, that it will be advantageous (even) to cross the great stream.

tuan.zh_hant: 益、損上益下，民說无疆。自上下下，其道大光。利有攸往、中正有慶，利涉大川、木道乃行。益動而巽，日進无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，與時偕行。
tuan.zh_hans: 益、损上益下，民说无疆。自上下下，其道大光。利有攸往、中正有庆，利涉大川、木道乃行。益动而巽，日进无疆。天施地生，其益无方。凡益之道，与时偕行。
tuan.en_legge: In Yi we see the upper (trigram) diminished, and the lower added to. The satisfaction of the people (in consequence of this) is without limit. What descends from above reaches to all below, so great and brilliant is the course (of its operation). That 'there will be advantage in every movement which shall be undertaken' appears from the central and correct (positions of the second and fifth lines), and the (general) blessing (the dispensing of which they imply). That 'it will be advantageous (even) to cross the great stream' appears from the action of wood (shown in the figure). Yi is made up of (the trigrams expressive of) movement and docility, (through which) there is daily advancement to an unlimited extent. We have (also) in it heaven dispensing and earth producing, leading to an increase without restriction of place. Everything in the method of this increase proceeds according to the requirements of the time.

image.zh_hant: 風雷益。君子以見善則遷，有過則改。
image.zh_hans: 风雷益。君子以见善则迁，有过则改。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) wind and that for thunder form Yi. The superior man, in accordance with this, when he sees what is good, moves towards it; and when he sees his errors, he turns from them.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows that it will be advantageous for its subject in his position to make a great movement. If it be greatly fortunate, no blame will be imputed to him.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'If the movement be greatly fortunate, no blame will be imputed to him:'—though it is not for one in so low a position to have to do with great affairs.

text.zh_hant: 或益之，十朋之龜弗克違。永貞吉。王用享于帝，吉。
text.zh_hans: 或益之，十朋之龟弗克违。永贞吉。王用享于帝，吉。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows parties adding to the stores of its subject ten pairs of tortoise shells whose oracles cannot be opposed. Let him persevere in being firm and correct, and there will be good fortune. Let the king, (having the virtues thus distinguished), employ them in presenting his offerings to God, and there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Parties add to his stores:'—they come from beyond (his immediate circle) to do so.

text.zh_hant: 益之，用凶事无咎。有孚，中行。告公用圭。
text.zh_hans: 益之，用凶事无咎。有孚，中行。告公用圭。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows increase given to its subject by means of what is evil, so that he shall (be led to good), and be without blame. Let him be sincere and pursue the path of the Mean, (so shall he secure the recognition of the ruler, like) an officer who announces himself to his prince by the symbol of his rank.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Increase is given by means of what is evil and difficult:'—as he has in himself (the qualities called forth).

text.zh_hant: 中行告公，從，利用為依遷國。
text.zh_hans: 中行告公，从，利用为依迁国。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject pursuing the due course. His advice to his prince is followed. He can with advantage be relied on in such a movement as that of removing the capital.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'His advice to his prince is followed:'—his (only) object in it being the increase (of the general good).

text.zh_hant: 有孚惠心，勿問，元吉。有孚惠我德。
text.zh_hans: 有孚惠心，勿问，元吉。有孚惠我德。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject with sincere heart seeking to benefit (all below). There need be no question about it; the result will be great good fortune. (All below) will with sincere heart acknowledge his goodness.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 有孚惠心、勿問之矣，惠我德、大得志也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 有孚惠心、勿问之矣，惠我德、大得志也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: '(The ruler) with sincere heart seeks to benefit (all below):'—there need be no question (about the result). '(All below) with sincere heart acknowledge (his goodness):'—he gets what he desires on a great scale.

text.zh_hant: 莫益之，或擊之，立心勿恆，凶。
text.zh_hans: 莫益之，或击之，立心勿恒，凶。
text.en_legge: In the sixth line, undivided, we see one to whose increase none will contribute, while many will seek to assail him. He observes no regular rule in the ordering of his heart. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 莫益之、偏辭也，或擊之、自外來也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 莫益之、偏辞也，或击之、自外来也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'To his increase none will contribute:'—this expresses but half the result. 'Many will seek to assail him:'—they will come from beyond (his immediate circle) to do so.

judgment.zh_hant: 揚于王庭，孚號有厲，告自邑。不利即戎，利有攸往。
judgment.zh_hans: 扬于王庭，孚号有厉，告自邑。不利即戎，利有攸往。
judgment.en_legge: Kwai requires (in him who would fulfil its meaning) the exhibition (of the culprit's guilt) in the royal court, and a sincere and earnest appeal (for sympathy and support), with a consciousness of the peril (involved in cutting off the criminal). He should (also) make announcement in his own city, and show that it will not be well to have recourse at once to arms. (In this way) there will be advantage in whatever he shall go forward to.

tuan.zh_hant: 夬、決也，剛決柔也。健而說，決而和。揚于王庭、柔乘五剛也，孚號有厲、其危乃光也。告自邑不利即戎、所尚乃窮也，利有攸往、剛長乃終也。
tuan.zh_hans: 夬、决也，刚决柔也。健而说，决而和。扬于王庭、柔乘五刚也，孚号有厉、其危乃光也。告自邑不利即戎、所尚乃穷也，利有攸往、刚长乃终也。
tuan.en_legge: Kwai is the symbol of displacing or removing. We see (in the figure) the strong (lines) displacing the weak. (We have in it the attributes of) strength and complacency. There is displacement, but harmony (continues). 'The exhibition (of the criminal's guilt) in the royal courtyard' is suggested by the (one) weak (line) mounted on the five strong lines. 'There is an earnest and sincere appeal (for sympathy and support), and a consciousness of the peril (involved in the undertaking):'—it is the realisation of this danger, which makes the method (of compassing the object) brilliant. 'He should make an announcement in his own city, and show that it will not be well to have recourse at once to arms:'—(if he have recourse to arms), what he prefers will (soon) be exhausted. 'There will be advantage in whatever he shall go forward to:'—when the growth of the strong (lines) has been completed, there will be an end (of the displacement).

image.zh_hant: 澤上於天，夬。君子以施祿及下，居德則忌。
image.zh_hans: 泽上于天，夬。君子以施禄及下，居德则忌。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) heaven and that for the waters of a marsh mounting above it form Kwai. The superior man, in accordance with this, bestows emolument on those below him, and dislikes allowing his gifts to accumulate (undispensed).

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject in (the pride of) strength advancing with his toes. He goes forward, but will not succeed. There will be ground for blame.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Without (being able to) succeed, he goes forward:'—this is an error.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject full of apprehension and appealing (for sympathy and help). Late at night hostile measures may be (taken against him), but he need not be anxious about them.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Though hostile measures be taken against him, he need not be anxious:'—he pursues the course of the due mean.

text.zh_hant: 壯于頄，有凶。君子夬夬，獨行遇雨、若濡，有慍无咎。
text.zh_hans: 壮于頄，有凶。君子夬夬，独行遇雨、若濡，有愠无咎。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject (about to advance) with strong (and determined) looks. There will be evil. (But) the superior man, bent on cutting off (the criminal), will walk alone and encounter the rain, (till he be hated by his proper associates) as if he were contaminated (by the others). (In the end) there will be no blame against him.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The superior man looks bent on cutting off the culprit:'--there will in the end be no error.

text.zh_hant: 臀无膚，其行次且。牽羊悔亡。聞言不信。
text.zh_hans: 臀无肤，其行次且。牵羊悔亡。闻言不信。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped, and who walks slowly and with difficulty. (If he could act) like a sheep led (after its companions), occasion for repentance would disappear. But though he hear these words, he will not believe them.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 其行次且、位不當也，聞言不信、聰不明也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 其行次且、位不当也，闻言不信、聪不明也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He walks slowly and with difficulty:'—he is not in the place appropriate to him. 'He hears these words, but does not believe them:'—he hears, but does not understand.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows (the small men like) a bed of purslain, which ought to be uprooted with the utmost determination. (The subject of the line having such determination), his action, in harmony with his central position, will lead to no error or blame.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'If his action be in harmony with his central position, there will be no error:'—but his standing in the due mean is not yet clearly displayed.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows its subject without any (helpers) on whom to call. His end will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There is the misery of having none on whom to call:'—the end will be that he cannot continue any longer.

judgment.en_legge: Kau shows a female who is bold and strong. It will not be good to marry (such) a female.

tuan.zh_hant: 姤、遇也，柔遇剛也。勿用取女、不可與長也。天地相遇，品物咸章也。剛遇中正，天下大行也。姤之時義大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 姤、遇也，柔遇刚也。勿用取女、不可与长也。天地相遇，品物咸章也。刚遇中正，天下大行也。姤之时义大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: Kau has the significance of unexpectedly coming on. (We see in it) the weak (line) coming unexpectedly on the strong ones. 'It will not be good to marry (such) a female:'—one (so symbolised) should not be long associated with. Heaven and earth meeting together (as here represented), all the variety of natural things become fully displayed. When a strong (line) finds itself in the central and correct position, (good government) will greatly prevail all under the sky. Great indeed is the significance of what has to be done at the time indicated by Kau!

image.zh_hant: 天下有風，姤。后以施命誥四方。
image.zh_hans: 天下有风，姤。后以施命诰四方。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) wind and that for the sky above it form Kau. The sovereign, in accordance with this, delivers his charges, and promulgates his announcements throughout the four quarters (of the kingdom).

text.zh_hant: 繫于金柅，貞吉。有攸往，見凶，羸豕孚蹢躅。
text.zh_hans: 系于金柅，贞吉。有攸往，见凶，羸豕孚蹢躅。
text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows how its subject should be kept (like a carriage) tied and fastened to a metal drag, in which case with firm correctness there will be good fortune. (But) if he move in any direction, evil will appear. He will be (like) a lean pig, which is sure to keep jumping about.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Tied and fastened to a metal drag:'—(this describes the arrest of) the weak (line) in its advancing course.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject with a wallet of fish. There will be no error. But it will not be well to let (the subject of the first line) go forward to the guests.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He has a wallet of fish:'—it is right for him not to allow (the subject of the first line) to get to the guests.

text.zh_hant: 臀无膚，其行次且，厲，无大咎。
text.zh_hans: 臀无肤，其行次且，厉，无大咎。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows one from whose buttocks the skin has been stripped so that he walks with difficulty. The position is perilous, but there will be no great error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He walks with difficulty:'—but his steps have not yet been drawn (into the course of the first line).

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject with his wallet, but no fish in it. This will give rise to evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The evil' indicated by there being 'no fish in the wallet' is owing to (the subject of the line) keeping himself aloof from the people.

text.zh_hant: 以杞包瓜，含章，有隕自天。
text.zh_hans: 以杞包瓜，含章，有陨自天。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, (shows its subject as) a medlar tree overspreading the gourd (beneath it). If he keep his brilliant qualities concealed, (a good issue) will descend (as) from Heaven.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 九五含章、中正也，有隕自天、志不舍命也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 九五含章、中正也，有陨自天、志不舍命也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The subject of the fifth line, undivided, keeps his brilliant qualities concealed:'—as is indicated by his central and correct position. '(The good issue) descends (as) from Heaven:'—his aim does not neglect the ordinances (of Heaven).

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows its subject receiving others on his horns. There will be occasion for regret, but there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He receives others on his horns:'—he is exhausted at his greatest height, and there will be cause for regret.

judgment.zh_hant: 亨，王假有廟。利見大人。亨，利貞，用大牲吉。利有攸往。
judgment.zh_hans: 亨，王假有庙。利见大人。亨，利贞，用大牲吉。利有攸往。
judgment.en_legge: In (the state denoted by) Zhui, the king will repair to his ancestral temple. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man; and then there will be progress and success, though the advantage must come through firm correctness. The use of great victims will conduce to good fortune; and in whatever direction movement is made, it will be advantageous.

tuan.zh_hant: 萃、聚也。順以說，剛中而應，故聚也。王假有廟、致孝享也，利見大人亨、聚以正也，用大牲吉、利有攸往、順天命也。觀其所聚而天地萬物之情可見矣。
tuan.zh_hans: 萃、聚也。顺以说，刚中而应，故聚也。王假有庙、致孝享也，利见大人亨、聚以正也，用大牲吉、利有攸往、顺天命也。观其所聚而天地万物之情可见矣。
tuan.en_legge: Zhui indicates (the condition of union, or) being collected. We have in it (the symbol of) docile obedience going on to (what is expressed by that of) satisfaction. There is the strong line in the central place, and rightly responded to. Hence comes the (idea of) union. 'The king will repair to his ancestral temple:'—with the utmost filial piety he presents his offerings (to the spirits of his ancestors). 'It will be advantageous to meet the great man, and there will then be prosperity and success:'—the union effected by him will be on and through what is correct. 'The use of great victims will conduce to good fortune; and in whatsoever direction movement is made, it will be advantageous:'—all is done in accordance with the ordinances of Heaven. When we look at the way in which the gatherings (here shown) take place, the natural tendencies (in the outward action) of heaven and earth and of all things can be seen.

image.zh_hant: 澤上於地，萃。君子以除戎器，戒不虞。
image.zh_hans: 泽上于地，萃。君子以除戎器，戒不虞。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing the) earth and that for the waters of a marsh raised above it form Shui. The superior man, in accordance with this, has his weapons of war put in good repair, to be prepared against unforeseen contingencies.

text.zh_hant: 有孚不終，乃亂乃萃，若號一握為笑，勿恤，往无咎。
text.zh_hans: 有孚不终，乃乱乃萃，若号一握为笑，勿恤，往无咎。
text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows its subject with a sincere desire (for union), but unable to carry it out, so that disorder is brought into the sphere of his union. If he cry out (for help to his proper correlate), all at once (his tears) will give place to smiles. He need not mind (the temporary difficulty); as he goes forward, there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'In consequence disorder is brought into the sphere of his union:'—his mind and aim are thrown into confusion.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject led forward (by his correlate). There will be good fortune, and freedom from error. There is entire sincerity, and in that case (even the small offerings of) the vernal sacrifice are acceptable.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is led forward; there will be good fortune, and freedom from error:'—(the virtue proper to) his central place has not undergone any change.

text.zh_hant: 萃如嗟如，无攸利，往无咎，小吝。
text.zh_hans: 萃如嗟如，无攸利，往无咎，小吝。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject striving after union and seeming to sigh, yet nowhere finding any advantage. If he go forward, he will not err, though there may be some small cause for regret.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'If he go forward, he will not err:'—in the subject of the topmost line there is humility and condescension.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject in such a state that, if he be greatly fortunate, he will receive no blame.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'If he be grandly fortunate, he will receive no blame:'—(this condition is necessary, because) his position is not the one proper to him.

text.zh_hant: 萃有位，无咎。匪孚，元、永貞悔亡。
text.zh_hans: 萃有位，无咎。匪孚，元、永贞悔亡。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows the union (of all) under its subject in the place of dignity. There will be no error. If any do not have confidence in him, let him see to it that (his virtue) be great, long-continued, and firmly correct, and all occasion for repentance will disappear.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There is the union (of all) under him in the place of dignity:'—(but) his mind and aim have not yet been brilliantly displayed.

text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject sighing and weeping; but there will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He sighs and weeps:'—he does not yet rest in his topmost position.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 元亨。用見大人，勿恤。南征吉。
judgment.zh_hans: 元亨。用见大人，勿恤。南征吉。
judgment.en_legge: Shang indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. Seeking by (the qualities implied in it) to meet with the great man, its subject need have no anxiety. Advance to the south will be fortunate.

tuan.zh_hant: 柔以時升，巽而順，剛中而應，是以大亨。用見大人勿恤、有慶也，南征吉、志行也。
tuan.zh_hans: 柔以时升，巽而顺，刚中而应，是以大亨。用见大人勿恤、有庆也，南征吉、志行也。
tuan.en_legge: (We find) the weak (line), as it finds the opportunity, ascending upwards. We have (the attribute) of flexibility and that of obedience; we have the strong line (below) and its proper correlate above:—these things indicate that there will be 'great progress and success.' 'Seeking (by the qualities implied in Shang) to meet with the great man, its subject need have no anxiety:'—there will be ground for congratulation. 'Advance to the south will be fortunate:'—his aim will be carried out.

image.zh_hant: 地中生木，升。君子以順德，積小以高大。
image.zh_hans: 地中生木，升。君子以顺德，积小以高大。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) wood and that for the earth with the wood growing in the midst of it form Shang. The superior man, in accordance with this, pays careful attention to his virtue, and accumulates the small developments of it till it is high and great.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards with the welcome (of those above him). There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is welcomed in his advance upwards, and there will be great good fortune:'—(the subjects of) the upper (trigram) are of the same mind with him.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject with that sincerity which will make even the (small) offerings of the vernal sacrifice acceptable. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The sincerity of the subject of the second line, undivided,' affords occasion for joy.

text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows its subject ascending upwards (as into) an empty city.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He advances upwards (as into) an empty city:'—he has no doubt or hesitation.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows its subject employed by the king to present his offerings on mount Khi. There will be good fortune; there will be no mistake.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The king employs him to prevent his offerings on mount Khi:'—such a service (of spiritual Beings) is according to (their mind).

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows its subject firmly correct, and therefore enjoying good fortune. He ascends the stairs (with all due ceremony).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is firmly correct, and will therefore enjoy good fortune. He ascends the stairs (with all due ceremony):'—he grandly succeeds in his aim.

text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows its subject advancing upwards blindly. Advantage will be found in a ceaseless maintenance of firm correctness.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He blindly advances upwards,' and is in the highest place:—but there is decay in store for him, and he will not (preserve) his riches.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.zh_hant: 亨。貞大人吉，无咎。有言不信。
judgment.zh_hans: 亨。贞大人吉，无咎。有言不信。
judgment.en_legge: In (the condition denoted by) Khwan there may (yet be) progress and success. For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune. He will fall into no error. If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good.

tuan.zh_hant: 困、剛揜也。險以說，困而不失其所，亨，其唯君子乎。貞大人吉、以剛中也，有言不信、尚口乃窮也。
tuan.zh_hans: 困、刚揜也。险以说，困而不失其所，亨，其唯君子乎。贞大人吉、以刚中也，有言不信、尚口乃穷也。
tuan.en_legge: In Khwan (we see) the strong (lines) covered and obscured (by the weak). We have in it (the attribute of) perilousness going on to that of satisfaction. Who is it but the superior man that, though straitened, still does not fail in making progress to his proper end? 'For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune:'—this is shown by the central positions of the strong (lines), 'If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good:'—to be fond of arguing or pleading is the way to be reduced to extremity.

image.zh_hant: 澤无水，困。君子以致命遂志。
image.zh_hans: 泽无水，困。君子以致命遂志。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) a marsh, and (below it that for a defile, which has drained the other dry so that there is) no water in it, form Khwan. The superior man, in accordance with this, will sacrifice his life in order to carry out his purpose.

text.zh_hant: 臀困于株木，入于幽谷，三歲不覿。
text.zh_hans: 臀困于株木，入于幽谷，三岁不觌。
text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows its subject with bare buttocks straitened under the stump of a tree. He enters a dark valley, and for three years has no prospect (of deliverance).

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He enters a dark valley:'—so benighted is he, and without clear vision.

text.zh_hant: 困于酒食，朱紱方來。利用享祀。征凶无咎。
text.zh_hans: 困于酒食，朱绂方来。利用享祀。征凶无咎。
text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows its subject straitened amidst his wine and viands. There come to him anon the red knee-covers (of the ruler). It will be well for him (to maintain his sincerity as) in sacrificing. Active operations (on his part) will lead to evil, but he will be free from blame.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is straitened amidst his wine and viands:'—(but) his position is central, and there will be ground for congratulation.

text.zh_hant: 困于石，據于蒺蔾，入于其宮，不見其妻，凶。
text.zh_hans: 困于石，据于蒺蔾，入于其宫，不见其妻，凶。
text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject straitened before a (frowning) rock. He lays hold of thorns. He enters his palace, and does not see his wife. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 據于蒺蔾、乘剛也，入于其宮不見其妻、不祥也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 据于蒺蔾、乘刚也，入于其宫不见其妻、不祥也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He lays hold of thorns:'—(this is suggested by the position of the line) above the strong (line). 'He enters his palace, and does not see his wife:'—this is inauspicious.

text.zh_hant: 來徐徐，困于金車，吝，有終。
text.zh_hans: 来徐徐，困于金车，吝，有终。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject proceeding very slowly (to help the subject of the first line), who is straitened by the carriage adorned with metal in front of him. There will be occasion for regret, but the end will be good.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 來徐徐、志在下也。雖不當位，有與也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 来徐徐、志在下也。虽不当位，有与也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He proceeds very slowly (to help the subject of the first line):'—his aim is directed to (help) that lower (line). Although he is not in his appropriate place, he and that other will (in the end) be together.

text.zh_hant: 劓刖，困于赤紱，乃徐有說，利用祭祀。
text.zh_hans: 劓刖，困于赤绂，乃徐有说，利用祭祀。
text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows its subject with his nose and feet cut off. He is straitened by (his ministers in their) scarlet aprons. He is leisurely in his movements, however, and is satisfied. It will be well for him to be (as sincere) as in sacrificing (to spiritual beings).

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 劓刖、志未得也，乃徐有說、以中直也，利用祭祀、受福也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 劓刖、志未得也，乃徐有说、以中直也，利用祭祀、受福也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'His nose and feet are cut off:'—his aim has not yet been gained. 'He is leisurely, however, in his movements, and is satisfied:'—his position is central and (his virtue) is correct. 'It will be well for him to be (as sincere as) in sacrificing:'—so shall he receive blessing.

text.zh_hant: 困于葛藟，于臲卼，曰動悔有悔，征吉。
text.zh_hans: 困于葛藟，于臲卼，曰动悔有悔，征吉。
text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows its subject straitened, as if bound with creepers; or in a high and dangerous position, and saying (to himself), 'If I move, I shall repent it.' If he do repent of former errors, there will be good fortune in his going forward.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 困于葛藟、未當也，動悔有悔、吉行也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 困于葛藟、未当也，动悔有悔、吉行也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is straitened as if bound with creepers:'—(his spirit and action) are unsuitable. '(He says), "If I' move, I 'shall repent: of ait. And he does repent (of former errors), which leads to good fortune:'—so he (now) goes on.

judgment.zh_hant: 改邑不改井，无喪无得。往來井井。汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶，凶。
judgment.zh_hans: 改邑不改井，无丧无得。往来井井。汔至，亦未繘井，羸其瓶，凶。
judgment.en_legge: (Looking at) Zing, (we think of) how (the site of) a town may be changed, while (the fashion of) its wells undergoes no change. (The water of a well) never disappears and never receives (any great) increase, and those who come and those who go can draw and enjoy the benefit. If (the drawing) have nearly been accomplished, but, before the rope has quite reached the water, the bucket is broken, this is evil.

tuan.zh_hant: 巽乎水而上水，井。井養而不窮也。改邑不改井、乃以剛中也。汔至、亦未繘井、未有功也，羸其瓶、是以凶也。
tuan.zh_hans: 巽乎水而上水，井。井养而不穷也。改邑不改井、乃以刚中也。汔至、亦未繘井、未有功也，羸其瓶、是以凶也。
tuan.en_legge: (We have the symbol of) wood in the water and the raising of the water; which (gives us the idea of) a well. A well supplies nourishment and is not (itself) exhausted. 'The site of a town may be changed, while the fashion of its wells undergoes no change:'—this is indicated by the central position of the strong lines (in the second and fifth places). 'The drawing is nearly accomplished, but the rope has not yet reached the water of the well:'—its service has not yet been accomplished. 'The bucket is broken:'—it is this that occasions evil.

image.zh_hant: 木上有水，井。君子以勞民勸相。
image.zh_hans: 木上有水，井。君子以劳民劝相。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for water form Zing. The superior man, in accordance with this, comforts the people, and stimulates them to mutual helpfulness.

text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows a well so muddy that men will not drink of it; or an old well to which neither birds (nor other creatures) resort.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 井泥不食、下也，舊井无禽、時舍也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 井泥不食、下也，旧井无禽、时舍也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A well so muddy that men will not drink of it:'—this is indicated by the low position (of the line), 'An old well to which the birds do not come:'—it has been forsaken in the course of time.

text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows a well from which by a hole the water escapes and flows away to the shrimps (and such small creatures among the grass), or one the water of which leaks away from a broken basket.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A well from which by a hole the water escapes, and flows away to the shrimps:'—(the subject of this second line has) none co-operating with him (above).

text.zh_hant: 井渫不食，為我心惻。可用汲，王明，並受其福。
text.zh_hans: 井渫不食，为我心恻。可用汲，王明，并受其福。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows a well, which has been cleared out, but is not used. Our hearts are sorry for this, for the water might be drawn out and used. If the king were (only) intelligent, both he and we might receive the benefit of it.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 井渫不食、行惻也，求王明、受福也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 井渫不食、行恻也，求王明、受福也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The well has been cleared out, but is not used:'—(even) passers-by would be sorry for this. A prayer is made 'that the king were intelligent:'—for then blessing would be received.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, divided, shows a well, the lining of which is well laid. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'A well the lining of which is well laid. There will be no error:'—the well has been put in good repair.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows a clear, limpid well, (the waters from) whose cold spring are (freely) drunk.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The waters from the cold spring are (freely) drunk:'—this is indicated by the central and correct position (of the line).

text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows (the water from) the well brought to the top, which is not allowed to be covered. This suggests the idea of sincerity. There will be great good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The great good fortune' at the topmost place indicates the grand accomplishment (of the idea in the hexagram).

judgment.zh_hant: 巳日乃孚。元亨，利貞，悔亡。
judgment.zh_hans: 巳日乃孚。元亨，利贞，悔亡。
judgment.en_legge: (What takes place as indicated by) Ko is believed in only after it has been accomplished. There will be great progress and success. Advantage will come from being firm and correct. (In that case) occasion for repentance will disappear.

tuan.zh_hant: 革、水火相息，二女同居，其志不相得曰革。巳日乃孚，革而信之。文明以說，大亨以正。革而當，其悔乃亡。天地革而四時成，湯武革命，順乎天而應乎人。革之時大矣哉！
tuan.zh_hans: 革、水火相息，二女同居，其志不相得曰革。巳日乃孚，革而信之。文明以说，大亨以正。革而当，其悔乃亡。天地革而四时成，汤武革命，顺乎天而应乎人。革之时大矣哉！
tuan.en_legge: In Ko (we see) water and fire extinguishing each other; (we see also) two daughters dwelling together, but with their minds directed to different objects:—(on account of these things) it is called (the hexagram of) Change. 'It is believed in (only) after it has been accomplished:'—when the change has been made, faith is accorded to it. (We have) cultivated intelligence (as the basis of) pleased satisfaction, (suggesting) 'great progress and success,' coming from what is correct. When change thus takes place in the proper way, 'occasion for repentance disappears.' Heaven and earth undergo their changes, and the four seasons complete their functions. Thang changed the appointment (of the line of Hsia to the throne), and Wu (that of the line of Shang), in accordance with (the will of) Heaven, and in response to (the wishes of) men. Great indeed is what takes place in a time of change.

image.zh_hant: 澤中有火，革。君子以治歷明時。
image.zh_hans: 泽中有火，革。君子以治历明时。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing the waters of) a marsh and that for fire in the midst of them form Ko. The superior man, in accordance with this, regulates his (astronomical) calculations, and makes clear the seasons and times.

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject (as if he were) bound with the skin of a yellow ox.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 鞏用黃牛、不可以有為也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 巩用黄牛、不可以有为也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is bound with (the skin of) a yellow ox:'—he should in his circumstances be taking action.

text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject making his changes after some time has passed. Action taken will be fortunate. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He makes his changes when some time has passed:'—what he does will be matter of admiration.

text.zh_hant: 征凶。貞厲。革言三就有孚。
text.zh_hans: 征凶。贞厉。革言三就有孚。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows that action taken by its subject will be evil. Though he be firm and correct, his position is perilous. If the change (he contemplates) have been three times fully discussed, he will be believed in.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The change (contemplated) has been three times fully discussed:'—to what else should attention (now) be directed?

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows occasion for repentance disappearing (from its subject). Let him be believed in; and though he change (existing) ordinances, there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The good fortune consequent on changing (existing) ordinances' is due to the faith reposed in his aims.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, undivided, shows the great man (producing his changes) as the tiger (does when he) changes (his stripes). Before he divines (and proceeds to action), faith has been reposed in him.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The great man produces his changes as the tiger does when he changes his stripes:'—their beauty becomes more brilliant.

text.zh_hant: 君子豹變，小人革面，征凶，居貞吉。
text.zh_hans: 君子豹变，小人革面，征凶，居贞吉。
text.en_legge: The sixth line, divided, shows the superior man producing his changes as the leopard (does when he) changes (his spots), while small men change their faces (and show their obedience). To go forward (now) would lead to evil, but there will be good fortune in abiding firm and correct.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 君子豹變、其文蔚也，小人革面、順以從君也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 君子豹变、其文蔚也，小人革面、顺以从君也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The superior man produces his changes as the leopard does when he changes his spots:'—their beauty becomes more elegant. 'Small men change their faces:'—they show themselves prepared to follow their ruler.

collated_with.edition: 四部叢刊本 王弼《周易注》 (Song edition), Kanseki Repository KR1a0006, branch SBCK

judgment.en_legge: Ting gives the intimation of great progress and success.

tuan.zh_hant: 鼎象也、以木巽火，亨飪也。聖人亨以享上帝，而大亨以養聖賢。巽而耳目聰明，柔進而上行，得中而應乎剛，是以元亨。
tuan.zh_hans: 鼎象也、以木巽火，亨饪也。圣人亨以享上帝，而大亨以养圣贤。巽而耳目聪明，柔进而上行，得中而应乎刚，是以元亨。
tuan.en_legge: In Ting we have (symbolically) the figure of a caldron. (We see) the (symbol of) wood entering into that of fire, which suggests the idea of cooking. The sages cooked their offerings in order to present them to God, and made great feasts to nourish their wise and able (ministers). We have (the symbol of) flexible obedience, and that (which denotes) ears quick of hearing and eyes clear-sighted. (We have also) the weak (line) advanced and acting above, in the central place, and responded to by the strong (line below). All these things give the idea of 'great progress and success.'

image.zh_hant: 木上有火，鼎。君子以正位凝命。
image.zh_hans: 木上有火，鼎。君子以正位凝命。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) wood and above it that for fire form Ting. The superior man, in accordance with this, keeps his every position correct, and maintains secure the appointment (of Heaven).

text.zh_hant: 鼎顛趾，利出否。得妾以其子，无咎。
text.zh_hans: 鼎颠趾，利出否。得妾以其子，无咎。
text.en_legge: The first line, divided, shows the caldron overthrown and its feet turned up. (But) there will be advantage in its getting rid of what was bad in it. (Or it shows us) the concubine (whose position is improved) by means of her son. There will be no error.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 鼎顛趾、未悖也，利出否、以從貴也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 鼎颠趾、未悖也，利出否、以从贵也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The caldron is overturned, and its feet turned upwards:'—but this is not (all) contrary (to what is right). 'There will be advantage in getting rid of what was bad:'—thereby (the subject of the line) will follow the more noble (subject of the fourth line).

text.zh_hant: 鼎有實，我仇有疾，不我能即，吉。
text.zh_hans: 鼎有实，我仇有疾，不我能即，吉。
text.en_legge: The second line, undivided, shows the caldron with the things (to be cooked) in it. (If its subject can say), 'My enemy dislikes me, but he cannot approach me,' there will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 鼎有實、慎所之也，我仇有疾、終无尤也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 鼎有实、慎所之也，我仇有疾、终无尤也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There is the caldron with the things (to be cooked) in it:'—let (the subject of the line) be careful where he goes. 'My enemy dislikes me:'—but there will in the end be no fault (to which he can point).

text.zh_hant: 鼎耳革，其行塞，雉膏不食，方雨，虧悔，終吉。
text.zh_hans: 鼎耳革，其行塞，雉膏不食，方雨，亏悔，终吉。
text.en_legge: The third line, undivided, shows the caldron with (the places of) its ears changed. The progress (of its subject) is (thus) stopped. The fat flesh of the pheasant (which is in the caldron) will not be eaten. But the (genial) rain will come, and the grounds for repentance will disappear. There will be good fortune in the end.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'There is the caldron with (the places for) its ears changed:'—(its subject) has failed in what was required of him (in his situation).

text.zh_hant: 鼎折足，覆公餗，其形渥，凶。
text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows the caldron with its feet broken; and its contents, designed for the ruler's use, overturned and spilt. Its subject will be made to blush for shame. There will be evil.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The contents designed for the ruler's use are overturned and spilt:'—how can (the subject of the line) be trusted?

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows the caldron with yellow ears and rings of metal in them. There will be advantage through being firm and correct.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The caldron has yellow ears:'—the central position (of the line) is taken as (a proof of) the solid (virtue of its subject).

text.en_legge: The sixth line, undivided, shows the caldron with rings of jade. There will be great good fortune, and all action taken will be in every way advantageous.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'The rings of jade' are at the very top:—the strong and the weak meet in their due proportions.

judgment.zh_hant: 亨。震來虩虩，笑言啞啞，震驚百里，不喪匕鬯。
judgment.zh_hans: 亨。震来虩虩，笑言哑哑，震惊百里，不丧匕鬯。
judgment.en_legge: Kan gives the intimation of ease and development. When (the time of) movement (which it indicates) comes, (the subject of the hexagram) will be found looking out with apprehension, and yet smiling and talking cheerfully. When the movement (like a crash of thunder) terrifies all within a hundred li, he will be (like the sincere worshipper) who is not (startled into) letting go his ladle and (cup of) sacrificial spirits.

tuan.zh_hant: 震亨。震來虩虩、恐致福也，笑言啞啞、後有則也，震驚百里、驚遠而懼邇也。出可以守宗廟社稷，以為祭主也。
tuan.zh_hans: 震亨。震来虩虩、恐致福也，笑言哑哑、后有则也，震惊百里、惊远而惧迩也。出可以守宗庙社稷，以为祭主也。
tuan.en_legge: Kan (gives the intimation of) ease and development. 'When the (time of) movement (which it indicates) comes, (its subject) will be found looking out with apprehension:'—that feeling of dread leads to happiness. 'And yet smiling and talking cheerfully:'—the issue (of his dread) is that he adopts (proper) laws (for his course). 'The movement (like a crash of thunder) terrifies all within a hundred li:'—it startles the distant and frightens the near. 'He will be like the sincere worshipper, who is not startled into letting go his ladle and cup of sacrificial spirits:'—he makes his appearance, and maintains his ancestral temple and the altars of the spirits of the land and grain, as presiding at all sacrifices.

image.zh_hant: 洊雷、震。君子以恐懼脩省。
image.zh_hans: 洊雷、震。君子以恐惧修省。
image.en_legge: (The trigram representing) thunder, being repeated, forms Kan. The superior man, in accordance with this, is fearful and apprehensive, cultivates (his virtue), and examines (his faults).

text.en_legge: The first line, undivided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, looking out and around with apprehension, and afterwards smiling and talking cheerfully. There will be good fortune.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 震來虩虩、恐致福也，笑言啞啞、後有則也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 震来虩虩、恐致福也，笑言哑哑、后有则也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'When the (time of) movement comes, he will be found looking out with apprehension:'—that feeling of dread leads to happiness. 'He yet smiles and talks cheerfully:'—the issue (of his dread) is that he adopts (proper) laws (for his course).

text.zh_hant: 震來厲，億喪貝，躋于九陵，勿逐，七日得。
text.zh_hans: 震来厉，亿丧贝，跻于九陵，勿逐，七日得。
text.en_legge: The second line, divided, shows its subject, when the movement approaches, in a position of peril. He judges it better to let go the articles (in his possession), and to ascend a very lofty height. There is no occasion for him to pursue after (the things he has let go); in seven days he will find them.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'When the movement approaches, he is in a position of peril:'—(a weak line) is mounted on a strong (one).

text.en_legge: The third line, divided, shows its subject distraught amid the startling movements going on. If those movements excite him to (right) action, there will be no mistake.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He is distraught amid the startling movements going on:'—(the third line) is in a position unsuitable to it.

text.en_legge: The fourth line, undivided, shows its subject, amid the startling movements, supinely sinking (deeper) in the mud.

xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Amid the startling movements, he sinks supinely in the mud:'—the light in him has not yet been brilliantly developed.

text.en_legge: The fifth line, divided, shows its subject going and coming amidst the startling movements (of the time), and always in peril; but perhaps he will not incur loss, and find business (which he can accomplish).

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 震往來厲、危行也，其事在中、大无喪也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 震往来厉、危行也，其事在中、大无丧也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'He goes and comes amid the startling movements, and (always) in peril:'—full of risk are his doings. 'What he has to do has to be done in his central position:'—far will he be from incurring any loss.

text.zh_hant: 震索索，視矍矍，征凶。震不于其躬、于其鄰、无咎。婚媾有言。
text.zh_hans: 震索索，视矍矍，征凶。震不于其躬、于其邻、无咎。婚媾有言。
text.en_legge: The topmost line, divided, shows its subject, amidst the startling movements (of the time), in breathless dismay and looking round him with trembling apprehension. If he take action, there will be evil. If, while the startling movements have not reached his own person and his neighbourhood, (he were to take precautions), there would be no error, though his relatives might (still) speak against him.

xiao_xiang.zh_hant: 震索索、中未得也，雖凶无咎、畏鄰戒也。
xiao_xiang.zh_hans: 震索索、中未得也，虽凶无咎、畏邻戒也。
xiao_xiang.en_legge: 'Amid the startling movements he is in breathless dismay:'—he has not found out (the course of) the due mean. 'Though evil (threatens), he will not fall into error:'—he is afraid of being warned by his neighbours.

emendations.base: 不喪匕鬯、出可以守宗廟
emendations.note: SBCK and Wikisource lack 不喪匕鬯
